### About ZYD Signage

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/about
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/about/index.md

Leading the international signage industry with precision since 2006.

Dalian Zhiyudao Signage & Tech. Co., Ltd. (ZYD) is a factory-direct manufacturer serving global B2B signage projects since 2006.

Our **20,000sqm production base** is equipped with CNC technology and structured production processes for architectural wayfinding and custom signs.

We can quote Door-to-Door (DDP) shipping when the destination and cargo details are confirmed. The agreed delivery scope, import duties, and taxes depend on the project-specific quotation.

![ZYD Factory Entrance](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/company-entrance.jpg)

Factory Entrance

#### What the factory produces

Production covers the signage families that a B2B project usually needs together: architectural wayfinding and Braille signage, medical care signage, halo-lit metal letters, ultra-slim LED light boxes, LED neon, metal and acrylic logo signs, outdoor pylon and monument signs, landscape furniture, waste bins, planter boxes, desk signs, portable A-frame signs, and complete coordinated signage systems. Every family is described on its own page in the [product range](https://www.zydsign.com/products), and the buying questions behind them are covered in the [signage guides](https://www.zydsign.com/guides).

Fabrication works in 304 stainless steel, galvanized steel and aluminium, alongside acrylic and LED components. Steel sheet is worked from 1.5mm stock, and painted finishes are applied as oven-baked paint at 180°C. Both state what the process works with rather than a performance rating, and the material route and finish for a given sign are settled per project against the environment it will stand in.

#### How a project moves through the factory

Every order follows the same eight stages, and each stage produces something the buyer can review: a technical brief, a 3D mockup, engineering drawings, fabricated parts, a finished surface, wired illumination, a quality record, and a packed shipment. Nothing is sent to production before the drawing set has been agreed.

1. 01Technical ConsultationExpert analysis of signage requirements and site conditions.
2. 02Precision 3D MockupVisualizing final aesthetics with industrial-grade 3D renderings.
3. 03Shop DrawingDetailed engineering schematics for structural and electrical systems.
4. 04CNC FabricationHigh-precision cutting and assembly using advanced automation.
5. 05Automotive CoatingDust-free finish application selected for the specified project environment.
6. 06LED IntegrationMulti-point wiring with LED modules selected for the project specification.
7. 07Illumination Quality ChecksProject-specific QC including illumination trials and final checks.
8. 08Global DDP ShippingSecure industrial crating and door-to-door logistics management.

#### How quality is confirmed

Quality is handled as a set of agreed checks rather than a single inspection at the end. The four points below are settled with the buyer and recorded against the project, so a supplier and a client are reviewing the same scope.

- Quality ControlEstablished quality processes, with the final check defined for the project rather than assumed.
- Electrical RequirementsReviewed against the conditions at the destination before the order is produced.
- Inspection ScopeAgreed with the buyer before production starts, so both sides know what is being checked.
- Material SelectionChosen against the specification and the environment the sign is made for.

#### Ordering and delivery basics

Minimum order is one unit, so a single reception sign and a multi-site rollout are both accepted. Typical production lead time is 7–14 days depending on scope and quantity, counted from the point the drawings and the artwork are agreed.

DDP may be quoted as a door-to-door scope once the destination and the cargo details are confirmed. The agreed delivery scope, import duties and taxes, and any warranty coverage, duration and exclusions are stated in the project quotation or supply agreement rather than assumed here.

Artwork and brand references are reviewed before quoting, and the 3D mockup stage exists so the intended appearance can be seen before fabrication. Start from the [contact form](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) with whatever drawings and constraints are already fixed.

Before You Write

#### What to send for a quotation

A signage quotation is built from the project, not from a product name, so the fastest route to a comparable price is a brief that states what is already fixed. A supplier can then price the same scope instead of guessing, and the open questions stay visible as open questions.

Send whatever exists today. Rough dimensions, a photograph of the wall or the ground, and a logo file are enough to start: the drawing set is developed with you during the technical consultation, and the free 3D mockup is produced before fabrication so the intended appearance can be reviewed first.

Minimum order is one unit and typical production lead time is 7–14 days from the point the artwork and the drawings are agreed, so an incomplete brief delays the start of production rather than the quotation. The [FAQ](https://www.zydsign.com/faq) answers the questions that arrive most often, and the [guides](https://www.zydsign.com/guides) cover material, illumination and procurement decisions in more detail.

##### Project brief checklist

- Artwork or logo file, with brand colour references
- Sign type, or the site and message if the type is still undecided
- Approximate overall dimensions, letter heights and quantity
- Indoor or outdoor placement, and the mounting surface
- Illumination preference: front-lit, halo-lit, non-illuminated, or undecided
- Material and finish direction, if one has been specified
- Photographs of the site and any access constraints
- Site city and country, delivery destination, and target timing

Unknown items are useful too: mark them for clarification and they are answered in the technical review rather than filled in with an assumption.

#### Frequently Asked Questions

Quick answers to common project inquiries.

Can you provide free 3D mockups?

Our engineering team can provide a 3D mockup for a project inquiry when the brief contains enough information to prepare one. The scope and format are confirmed with the project before production.

What file formats do I need to provide for my logo?

We prefer vector files such as .AI, .EPS, .SVG, or high-resolution .PDF. These ensure the highest precision for CNC cutting and fabrication.

What is the minimum order quantity for custom signage?

The minimum order quantity (MOQ) is 1 piece for the listed custom signage products. Your quotation can cover one sign or a larger project quantity, depending on the brief.

What information do you need to prepare a signage quotation?

Please provide the artwork, approximate dimensions, quantity, finish, lighting requirement, and ship-to destination. These inputs help define the fabrication and delivery scope instead of relying on a headline estimate.

How much does custom signage cost?

There is no single price for custom signage because the scope varies by artwork, dimensions, quantity, materials and finish, lighting, packing, shipping, and installation responsibility. Share those project inputs so the quotation can describe a comparable scope.

How should I choose materials for an outdoor sign?

Material selection should follow the project environment and design brief, including exposure, appearance, finish, fabrication, drainage, cleaning access, and maintenance. The right choice is project-specific rather than a universal material recommendation.

What information is needed for a DDP shipping quotation?

DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) is a door-to-door delivery model that includes import duties and taxes within the agreed delivery scope. Freight and duties must be calculated from the destination and cargo details, so please share the ship-to location, dimensions, quantity, and other available project information.

What is the standard lead time?

Typical production lead time is 7–14 days depending on project complexity, artwork, quantity, and finish. Large-scale rollout projects are phased according to your schedule.

Do you provide detailed installation drawings?

Installation templates and technical drawings can be prepared when they are included in the project scope. They show the agreed mounting points and electrical connections for the specified sign.

What is International DDP Shipping?

DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) is a door-to-door delivery model in which the agreed delivery scope includes import clearance, duties, and taxes. Availability and the delivered scope are quoted from the destination and cargo details.

Are your signs durable in coastal environments?

Coastal projects need a material and finish review based on exposure, appearance, fabrication, drainage, cleaning access, and maintenance. 304 stainless steel or another route may be considered when it fits the confirmed project brief; no material is a universal guarantee against corrosion.

What are your warranty terms?

Any warranty coverage, duration, and exclusions are stated in the project quotation or supply agreement. They depend on the supplied scope and should be confirmed before production.

Do you offer engineering support for structural calculations?

Yes, for large-scale monument signs and pylons, our structural engineers can provide wind load calculations and foundation specifications tailored to your local environment.

#### Still have questions?

Our technical sales engineers are ready to assist with your specific project requirements.

### Signage Guides

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/guides
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/guides/index.md

Practical buying and technical guides for custom signage projects.

#### What these guides cover

Twenty-three guides cover the decisions that sit in front of a signage order: how the illuminated routes compare, how raceway and individually mounted channel letters differ, what shapes a channel letter quotation, how material and finish routes are chosen, how a complete site package is procured stage by stage, how a low-bid tender fails at acceptance, how imported signage clears customs and hands over to an installer, how tactile and Braille signage is planned and how custom Braille door signs are specified, and how a mall, an industrial park or a hotel becomes one coordinated signage system.

#### How to read them

Each guide states what belongs to the buyer and what belongs to the supplier. Project-specific items such as dimensions, materials, finishes, illumination and delivery scope are presented as decisions to confirm with a supplier rather than as universal figures, because the same sign type can be specified in several ways for different sites.

#### Where to go next

Guides answer the buying questions; the [product range](https://www.zydsign.com/products) shows what is manufactured for each sign type, and the [case studies](https://www.zydsign.com/projects) show how those sign types were coordinated on real sites. When the brief is ready, the technical review starts from the [contact form](https://www.zydsign.com/contact).

#### Fourteen product families from one factory

The range covers architectural wayfinding and Braille signage, medical care signage, halo-lit metal letters, ultra-slim LED light boxes, LED neon, metal and acrylic logo signs, outdoor pylon and monument signs, landscape furniture, and street furniture such as waste bins, planter boxes, desk signs and A-frame signs. They are listed together because a project usually buys several at once and can take them from one factory under one drawing set and one delivery scope.

#### Start from the site, not the product name

Whether a sign stands indoors or outdoors, mounts on a wall or on the ground, and how far away it has to be read decides more of the specification than the product name does. The material routes used across the range are 304 stainless steel, galvanized steel and aluminium, and illumination can be front-lit, halo-lit or left out altogether. The guide to [choosing the right sign for a business](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business) works through that comparison against the real site.

Where the work is going out to tender, the guide to [low-bid signage tenders](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/signage-procurement-low-bid-pitfalls) explains why two prices for the same sign are rarely the same scope.

### Case Studies

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/projects
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/projects/index.md

#### Where the signage work has been delivered

The case studies published here cover commercial complexes, industrial parks and retail sites. The factory work is broader than the projects that can be shown: medical care signage for hospitals, clinics and other healthcare facilities is produced alongside landscape and site furniture — benches, planters, waste bins and other coordinated outdoor elements — for public and private developments.

A project page is published once the client release allows the photographs and the scope to be shown, so medical and landscape projects are described here as coverage rather than named individually. The work itself follows the same route as the projects below: the sign types are planned together, the material and finish are settled against the site, and the delivery scope is confirmed before production.

#### What these projects have in common

Each case study describes a signage system rather than a single sign: a commercial complex that needed exterior identification through to interior floor directories, an industrial park that needed gateways, road and building identification coordinated across one large site, and a shopping centre that needed festive atrium installations built, lit and installed overnight. The pattern they share is that the sign types were planned together before anything was fabricated.

#### What a case study lets you check

Read one as a checklist of scope: the site type and its constraints, the sign types that were coordinated, the material and finish direction, the structural and installation conditions, the delivery arrangement, and who was responsible for each stage. If a comparable situation appears in your own brief, it tells you which questions to settle before requesting a quotation.

#### How to use them in a brief

A case study is evidence of scope, not a specification to copy, because dimensions, materials and finishes are settled per project. Point to the closest comparable situation in your inquiry and it becomes a shortcut to the right questions. The [guide to choosing the right sign](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business) covers the rest of the decision, and the [contact form](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) is where a comparable project gets reviewed.

![Custom acrylic desk sign](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/acrylic-desk-sign.jpg)

Acrylic desk signs: the short answer

#### A sign that stands where the conversation happens

An acrylic desk sign is a free-standing sign that sits on a counter, reception desk, or meeting table and carries the brand mark, a name, or a short message. It is the right choice where a wall sign would sit too far behind the viewer, or where the counter itself is the focal point of the space. The build is settled against the artwork and the surface it will stand on before production starts.

MOQ 1

Single-unit orders accepted

7–14 days

Typical production lead time

DDP

Delivered to your destination

Typical Applications

#### Where a desk sign earns its place

The common thread is a counter with someone standing at it. Wall signage identifies a building or a department from a distance, while a desk sign works at arm's length.

01

##### Reception & Front Desk

Puts the company mark on the counter the visitor is already looking at, instead of on a wall behind it.

02

##### Hotel & Showroom Counters

Carries the brand on a check-in or sales counter where guests are standing and waiting.

03

##### Meeting & Conference Tables

Identifies a room, a table, or a named seat when the room itself is shared or reconfigurable.

04

##### Trade Shows & Pop-Ups

Moves with the stand between venues, which suits temporary counters and short-term retail space.

Specification & Options

#### Confirmed against your project, not assumed

Desk signs are quoted from the artwork and the counter they will stand on, so the options below are settled with you rather than published as fixed figures. Send the brief and we will come back with a build to review.

Format

##### Free-standing counter sign

Stands on the desk or counter on its own base. Single-sided and double-sided reading are available options; which one is right depends on how people approach the counter.

Base & Face

##### Acrylic construction

Acrylic is the material family for this product. Base format, face build, edge treatment, and any accent layer are confirmed against the artwork and the surface the sign stands on.

Branding

##### Artwork-led graphics

The mark, name, or short message is built from the artwork supplied. Colour is matched to the brand references provided, and the graphic method is confirmed with the project.

Illumination

##### Available as an option

Desk signs can be specified with or without illumination. Whether a lit version suits the counter, and how it would be powered, are available options confirmed with the project.

Related Reading

#### Where a counter sign sits in the wider package

A desk sign is usually one line of a larger signage brief, and the choice between a counter sign, a wall sign and a pylon sign follows the site rather than a preference. The guide to [choosing the right sign for a business](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business) sets out how monument, building, wayfinding and illuminated signs are compared against the site, the viewing distance and the message.

Acrylic is the material family for this product, while the sheet routes discussed elsewhere on this site are 304 stainless steel, galvanized steel and aluminium. The [materials and finishes guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/signage-material-selection-guide) explains how a material route and a surface finish are reviewed against exposure, appearance, cleaning access and the background the sign will be seen against.

The build follows the same route as the rest of the range: artwork review, fabrication, finishing and a project-specific check before packing. The guide to the [signage manufacturing process](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/custom-signage-manufacturing-process) walks through those steps, so a buyer can see which stages the quotation covers.

Questions

#### Desk sign FAQs

##### What is an acrylic desk sign used for?

It is a free-standing sign that stands on a counter, reception desk, or meeting table rather than on a wall, so the brand mark or a name sits at reading distance from the person in front of it. Reception, front-of-house, hotel check-in, and showroom counters are the usual settings.

##### Can a desk sign be read from both sides?

Single-sided and double-sided reading are both available options. Which one suits the counter depends on whether people approach from one side or from both, and that is confirmed with the project before production.

##### How is the right desk sign build decided?

From the artwork, the surface the sign will stand on, and how it is expected to be handled. Base format, face build, edge finish, and any accent layer are confirmed against those factors rather than assumed in advance.

##### What is the minimum order and lead time for a desk sign?

Minimum order is 1 unit and typical production lead time is 7–14 days depending on artwork, quantity, and finish. DDP delivery and any warranty terms are confirmed in the project quotation.

#### Planning a desk or counter sign?

Send the artwork, the number of units, and the counter or desk it will stand on for a project-specific review.

### Architectural Wayfinding Systems

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/products/architectural-wayfinding-system
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/products/architectural-wayfinding-system/index.md

Directional signage systems for airports, hospitals, campuses, and mixed-use developments.

[GET A QUOTE](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) Check Feasibility

What to send for an architectural wayfinding system

- • Site or floor plans
- • Sign types and quantities
- • Artwork or brand standards
- • Mounting conditions and ship-to country

Send what you have: artwork, approximate dimensions, quantity, finish or lighting direction, mounting/site photos, and ship-to country.

![Architectural Wayfinding System](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/hero-wayfinding.jpg)

Wayfinding systems: the short answer

A wayfinding system organizes every sign type into one hierarchy so a visitor can move from arrival to destination without hesitation. The work begins with the journey and decision points, then defines panels, mounting, and finishes as a matched family rather than a collection of separate signs.

#### How is a wayfinding system planned for a large site?

Planning starts with the visitor journey: arrival, parking, first decision point, corridors, and final destination. Each decision point defines what the sign must say and how far ahead it must be read, which then sets the panel sizes and mounting. Our selection guide explains how to match sign formats to the site and viewer.

[Read the sign-selection guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business)

#### Which materials suit interior and exterior wayfinding?

Interior panels are frequently aluminum or acrylic with printed or applied graphics, while exterior and street-level elements need a finish route suited to weather and cleaning. Where an exposed metal finish is required, 304 stainless steel is a common selection. The material guide compares the exposed-steel and coated-steel routes.

[Review outdoor material options](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### How is a wayfinding quotation prepared?

A comparable quotation needs the site plan or floor plans, the list of sign types and quantities, the mounting conditions, the artwork or brand standards, and any accessibility requirement the project specifies. Sending those items together lets the schedule and scope be reviewed in one pass.

[Send your project brief](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) [Plan accessible signage](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/ada-braille-signage-planning-guide)

#### How does wayfinding coordinate with entry signage?

Wayfinding rarely stands alone: entry monuments, illuminated letters, and light boxes often carry the same brand language into the building. Coordinating them as one program keeps the finish, typography, and hardware consistent and simplifies installation across the site.

[See entry monument signage](https://www.zydsign.com/products/outdoor-pylon-monument-sign)

#### Specifications with selection logic

Each item is a decision input for a wayfinding program. Confirm the journey, mounting, and accessibility requirement before production.

##### Sign family

- • Overhead, projecting, and wall-mounted panels
- • Freestanding directories and map boards
- • Tactile and Braille options when specified

##### Panels & finish

- • Aluminum and acrylic panel construction
- • 304 stainless steel for exposed metal elements
- • Powder coating in specified RAL colors

##### Mounting

- • Ceiling-hung and wall-bracket assemblies
- • Flush mounting where the wall allows
- • Fixing layout confirmed from the site survey

##### Illumination & durability

- • Optional LED modules selected for the project specification
- • Power supplies selected for the project specification where lit
- • Environmental rating reviewed for the exterior application
- • Warranty terms confirmed in the project quotation

##### Factory Advantage

Direct manufacturing from our 20,000sqm base in Dalian, established in 2006, keeps panel fabrication and finishing under one quality-control process.

DDP Shipping by Quotation

MOQ: 1

Lead Time: 7–14 days

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What is architectural wayfinding and how is it planned?

Architectural wayfinding is the system of signs, maps, and markers that helps people decide where to go inside a building or campus. Planning starts from the visitor journey and decision points, not from individual sign panels, so the hierarchy stays consistent from the entrance to the final destination.

##### How do you handle accessibility requirements in a wayfinding system?

Accessibility requirements vary by country, building type, and the authority having jurisdiction, so they are confirmed for each project before production. We can build tactile and Braille options, mounting heights, and contrast into the schedule when the project brief specifies them. Our published guidance is a reference and does not replace a local code review.

##### What is the lead time for a wayfinding system?

Typical production lead time is 7–14 days depending on the number of sign types, quantity, and artwork. Phased rollouts are scheduled against your construction program.

#### Planning a wayfinding program?

Send the site or floor plans, sign types, quantities, and mounting conditions for a project-specific review.

### Complete Signage Systems

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/products/complete-signage-system
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/products/complete-signage-system/index.md

Coordinated sign programs for chain rollouts and multi-site brand projects.

[GET A QUOTE](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) Check Feasibility

What to send for a complete signage system

- • Site list and rollout sequence
- • Sign types and quantities per site
- • Artwork or brand standards
- • Mounting/site photos and ship-to country

Send what you have: artwork, approximate dimensions, quantity, finish or lighting direction, mounting/site photos, and ship-to country.

![Complete Signage System](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/cat-system.jpg)

Complete systems: the short answer

A complete signage system delivers every sign type in a project as one coordinated package, so the brand looks the same on the facade, in the car park, and inside the building. Choose it when many elements must be repeated across sites without the finish or hardware drifting between suppliers.

#### Which sign types belong in one program?

A full program typically combines entry monuments or pylons, illuminated channel letters, light boxes, wayfinding, and interior logo and room signage. Grouping them matters because a chain rollout needs the same typography, color, and mounting logic at every site. Our selection guide explains how each format earns its place.

[Read the sign-selection guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business)

#### How is consistency maintained across multiple locations?

Consistency comes from a locked specification: fixed materials, finishes, and graphic standards that every site order follows rather than re-deciding each location. Exposed metal elements follow one material route, which is often 304 stainless steel outdoors. The material guide covers how that compares with coated steel.

[Review material selection logic](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### What information is needed to quote a full program?

Send the site list, the required sign types and quantities per site, the brand standards or artwork, the mounting conditions, and the opening sequence. Providing the full package in one brief lets the program be priced, scheduled, and phased as a single coordinated scope.

[Send your project brief](https://www.zydsign.com/contact)

#### How is a multi-site rollout phased and shipped?

Rollouts are scheduled by site or opening date, with element groups produced and packed in the order they are needed on site. DDP delivery can be quoted into the program after the destination and cargo details are reviewed, with freight, clearance, and duties stated in the agreed scope.

[Explore coordinated wayfinding](https://www.zydsign.com/products/architectural-wayfinding-system)

#### Specifications with selection logic

Each item is a decision input for a coordinated program. Confirm the scope, standards, and phasing before production.

##### Program scope

- • Exterior entry and building identification
- • Illuminated letters and light boxes
- • Wayfinding and interior brand elements

### Custom Front-Lit Channel Letters

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-channel-letters
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-channel-letters/index.md

Letters whose face is the light source, fabricated in acrylic and sheet metal with concealed LED modules and a project-specific finish.

[GET A QUOTE](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) Check Feasibility

What to send for custom front-lit channel letters

- • Vector artwork and letter size
- • Quantity and overall run
- • Wall material and mounting photo
- • Face material, finish and ship-to country

Send what you have: artwork, approximate dimensions, quantity, finish or lighting direction, mounting/site photos, and ship-to country.

![Front-Lit Channel Letters](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/cat-illuminated.jpg)

Front-lit channel letters: the short answer

A front-lit channel letter is built so that the illuminated surface is the face: the letter body holds the LED modules and the light leaves through the acrylic face, which makes the letter itself the bright element. Choose it when the letters have to read as branded signs in daylight and at night, rather than throwing light onto the wall behind them.

#### How are front-lit channel letters built?

The letter is formed from sheet metal to create a body with a return, the LED modules are mounted inside that return and wired back to a power supply, and a translucent acrylic face is fitted and trimmed. The face material, the depth of the return and the module spacing are set together, because those three decide whether the face reads evenly or shows the light source. Nothing goes to production before the shop drawing records them.

[Compare front-lit and halo-lit letters](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/front-lit-vs-halo-lit-channel-letters)

#### Which materials suit outdoor front-lit letters?

Letter bodies for exterior work are usually 304 stainless steel, aluminum or coated sheet, with the face in translucent acrylic and the trim in a matching or contrasting metal finish. The material route and the fixing detail are chosen against the exposure of the site, so a coastal or heavily weathered location is specified differently from a sheltered one. The material comparison covers how the sheet routes differ.

[Review outdoor material options](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### What information is needed for a front-lit letter quotation?

A comparable quotation is built from vector artwork, the letter height and overall run, the quantity, the wall material, the mounting height and the finish direction, with the face material stated because it changes the construction. Site photos help confirm the standoff and the wiring route. The cost guide sets out how each of those inputs moves the price.

[See what shapes the cost](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-much-do-custom-channel-letters-cost)

#### How are illumination and service access specified?

Lighting is specified as part of the build rather than added afterwards: module type, spacing and the power supply position are listed on the drawing, and the face or a service panel is detailed so a letter can be opened without taking the whole sign off the wall. How the face, return and trim materials are reviewed together is covered in the material guide.

[Read the material guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/signage-material-selection-guide)

#### Specifications with selection logic

Each item is a decision input for a front-lit letter. Confirm the face, the return depth and the mounting route before production.

##### Letter face

- • Translucent acrylic, the illuminated surface
- • Face material chosen against the required light spread
- • Trim fitted around the face edge

##### Letter body

- • 304 stainless steel for exposed outdoor letters
- • Aluminum for lighter letter bodies

- • Power supplies selected for the project specification

Related Reading

#### Two illuminated constructions, one decision

Front-lit letters light the face; halo-lit (rear-glow) letters leave the face dark and light the wall behind it. The two are often specified for different parts of the same project — a bright front-lit facade and a restrained rear-glow entrance — and reading them side by side is usually how that split is settled. The [halo-lit (rear-glow) letters](https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-halo-lit-letters) page shows the other construction.

Once the construction is fixed, the remaining questions are commercial and procedural: what the price is built from, how a low bid can pass acceptance while missing the scope, and what the production stages are between drawing and packing. The [low-bid tender guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/signage-procurement-low-bid-pitfalls) and the [manufacturing process guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/custom-signage-manufacturing-process) cover those, and the [contact form](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) is where a front-lit letter set gets reviewed.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What is a front-lit channel letter?

A front-lit channel letter is a fabricated letter with a translucent face that is lit from inside the letter body. The light passes through the face, so the letter itself glows while the wall behind it stays dark. That is the opposite of a halo-lit (rear-glow) letter, where the face stays unlit and the light is thrown back onto the wall.

##### How is the illumination built inside the letter?

The letter body carries LED modules mounted on the interior of the return and wired back to a remote power supply. Module spacing and the depth of the return are set against the letter size and the face material, so the face reads evenly instead of in bright patches. The layout is drawn on the shop drawing that precedes production.

##### What are the face, return and trim made from?

The face is normally translucent acrylic, and the return and the trim are formed from sheet metal — aluminum or stainless steel are the usual routes, with coated sheet where a painted finish is specified. The trim is the visible edge around the face, so its material and finish are a design decision as much as a construction one.

##### Which finishes can be specified for the letter body?

Brushed or mirror stainless steel are common on architectural work, and a letter body can be powder coated in specified RAL colors. The return is the part seen from the side, so its finish is usually chosen against the facade. Face material and body finish are confirmed together on the shop drawing.

##### How are front-lit letters mounted to a wall?

Letters are mounted either on a raceway or on individual brackets. A raceway carries the wiring and gives a consistent standoff, while individual mounting suits letter sets that follow a curve or an irregular elevation. Which route is used depends on how the wiring has to reach each letter and how flat the wall is.

##### Can front-lit letters be used outdoors or in coastal locations?

Outdoor letter sets are a common request, and the material route and fixing detail are chosen with the exposure in mind. A coastal or heavily exposed site calls for a different specification than a sheltered one, so the route is confirmed per project rather than assumed from the letter type. Share the location and the wall condition with the brief.

##### How is brightness uniformity controlled across a letter?

Uniformity comes from the module spacing, the depth of the return and the face material together. A deeper return with closer module spacing gives a more even face, while a shallow return can show the light source as a hot spot. The intended effect is confirmed before fabrication.

##### Can a single module or one letter be serviced on site?

Service access is planned while the letter is designed. Letters are usually built so the face or a service panel can be opened without removing the whole sign, and the power supply is positioned where it can be reached. Access, wiring route and power supply positions are recorded on the drawing set.

##### What information is needed for a front-lit letter quotation?

A comparable quotation needs the artwork in vector form, the letter height, the overall run and the quantity, plus the wall material, the mounting height and the finish direction. State the face material as well, because it changes the construction. Send those details with the brief and the engineering review follows.

##### What are the MOQ and the lead time for front-lit letters?

Minimum order is one unit. Typical production lead time is 7–14 days depending on letter count, size, finish and lighting configuration, and larger rollout projects are phased against your schedule.

#### Planning front-lit letters?

Send the artwork, letter height, quantity, wall material and face direction for a project-specific review.

### Custom Halo-Lit Metal Letters

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-halo-lit-letters
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-halo-lit-letters/index.md

Rear-glow illumination for architectural branding, fabricated as dimensional metal letters with LED modules.

[GET A QUOTE](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) Check Feasibility

What to send for custom halo-lit metal letters

- • Vector artwork and letter size
- • Quantity and overall run
- • Wall material and mounting photo
- • Finish, lighting direction and ship-to country

Send what you have: artwork, approximate dimensions, quantity, finish or lighting direction, mounting/site photos, and ship-to country.

![Halo-Lit Signage](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/cat-illuminated.jpg)

Halo-lit letters: the short answer

Halo-lit letters keep the face dark and throw light backward onto the wall, creating a floating rear-glow effect instead of an illuminated face. Choose them when the wall itself should carry the light and the brand calls for a more restrained, architectural look rather than a bright front-lit face.

#### When should a project choose halo-lit instead of front-lit letters?

Halo lighting works well where the wall is part of the design: stone, brick, dark cladding, or any surface that benefits from reflected light. Front-lit letters read more strongly from a distance and in daylight, so the choice usually follows the viewing context and the intended visual character. Our comparison guide walks through both routes side by side.

[Compare front-lit and halo-lit letters](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/front-lit-vs-halo-lit-channel-letters)

#### Which materials suit rear-glow dimensional letters?

Letter bodies are typically fabricated in stainless steel, aluminum, or coated sheet, with the finish chosen to match the facade and the maintenance plan. 304 stainless steel is a common outdoor route, while powder coating in specified RAL colors gives the brand control over the visible metal. The material guide covers the coated-steel alternative in detail.

[Review outdoor material options](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### What information is needed for a halo-lit letter quotation?

A comparable quotation needs the artwork in vector form, the letter height and overall run length, the quantity, the wall material, and the required finish. Site photos and the mounting height help confirm the standoff and wiring route. Send those details with the brief and the engineering review follows.

[Send your project brief](https://www.zydsign.com/contact)

#### Can halo-lit letters be combined with other sign types?

Yes. Rear-glow letters are often paired with entry monuments, illuminated light boxes, or interior lobby signage so one brand language carries from the facade to the reception wall. Delivering those elements together keeps the finish and lighting consistent across the project.

[See matched LED light boxes](https://www.zydsign.com/products/ultra-slim-led-light-box)

#### Specifications with selection logic

Each item is a decision input for rear-glow construction. Confirm the wall, finish, and lighting requirement before production.

| Parameter | Range we build | What it suits — and where the limit is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Letter height | 100 mm minimum; no fixed maximum | Rear-glow construction needs enough return and stroke width to conceal the modules and spread the light. Letters larger than a single fabricated unit are built in sections with internal framing, and the split is fixed on the drawing. |
| Letter depth (return) | 25–100 mm | Depth sets the standoff from the wall and therefore how wide the halo reads. Deeper returns widen the glow and increase the load on the fixing, so the depth is agreed against the wall type and the intended effect. |
| Colour temperature | 3000–10000 K | 3000–4000 K reads warm, 4000–5000 K neutral, around 6500 K daylight, and above that very cool. The wall colour and finish also change how the glow reads, so the final value is checked on a sample. |
| Input voltage | 110–240 V AC | Universal-input power supplies cover 110 V and 230 V destinations; the LED side runs on low-voltage DC. The plug, circuit, isolation and any local approval remain destination requirements. |
| Mounting | Screw fixing (studs or flange) | Suits substrates that accept mechanical fixings — concrete, masonry, metal panel and timber. Curtain wall, stone cladding, EIFS and glazed surfaces need a fixing detail agreed on the drawing rather than a default screw. |

These are manufacturing ranges, not a quotation. The final dimension, depth, colour temperature and fixing detail are fixed on the approved drawing before production, and the quotation states what is included.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What is the difference between halo-lit and front-lit channel letters?

Halo-lit letters illuminate from behind, so the light reflects off the mounting surface and forms a soft glow around each letter while the face stays unlit. Front-lit letters light the face itself. Halo-lit construction suits darker or textured walls and a more restrained architectural look.

##### Can halo-lit letters be mounted on any wall surface?

The mounting surface affects the result, because the glow depends on light reflecting back from the wall. Smooth, light, or matte surfaces behave differently from dark or highly textured ones, and standoff depth changes the halo effect. Share the wall material and a photo with the brief so the mounting approach can be confirmed. Screw fixing with studs or flange is the standard route; where the wall cannot accept a mechanical fixing, the detail is agreed on the drawing before production.

##### What is the lead time for custom halo-lit letters?

Typical production lead time is 7–14 days depending on letter count, size, finish, and lighting configuration. Large rollout projects are phased according to your schedule.

LED neon signs: the short answer

Choose LED neon when the brand mark should glow in a hand-drawn, continuous-line form on an interior wall or window. The flexible tubing follows script and logo outlines closely, mounts light on most surfaces, and gives a softer decorative effect than rigid illuminated letters or panels.

#### When is LED neon the right choice for a brand?

LED neon suits interiors where the mark should feel expressive and decorative rather than architectural: reception walls, hospitality features, retail windows, and event backdrops. For facades and long-view identification, dimensional letters or illuminated panels usually perform better. The general selection guide explains how to match the format to the space.

#### How is artwork prepared for flexible neon tubing?

The design is simplified into continuous paths that the tubing can follow, so very fine detail and tight inner corners are usually adjusted. Vector artwork gives the cleanest starting point. The review confirms which strokes stay open and how the power feed and controller are hidden.

Share the wall material, the mounting height, and whether a visible or concealed power feed is preferred, plus the required color and any dimming or animation requirement. Those details determine the backing and the driver selection, and they keep the quotation comparable between suppliers.

#### Comparing illumination routes before you commit

Illuminated signage splits into routes that look different at night and need different mounting backgrounds, so the effect is worth settling before artwork is finalised. The comparison of [front-lit and halo-lit letters](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/front-lit-vs-halo-lit-channel-letters) explains how the two effects differ and what each one asks of the surface behind it, which is the same question a neon feature raises on an interior wall.

Neon tube is usually mounted on a backing panel or a prepared surface, so the panel material and its finish are part of the brief rather than an afterthought. The [materials and finishes guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/signage-material-selection-guide) covers how that route is chosen alongside the light source and the viewing environment.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What is the difference between LED neon and traditional glass neon?

LED neon uses flexible tubing with embedded LEDs rather than bent glass tubes filled with gas. The result is a comparable glow in a shatter-resistant form that is lighter to mount and easier to route around shapes, which is why it is common for interior branding and event work.

##### Where can LED neon signs be installed?

Most LED neon projects are interior: reception walls, retail windows, hospitality spaces, and event displays. Outdoor or wet-area use needs a different build and power arrangement, so confirm the location and exposure with the brief before quoting.

##### What is the lead time for custom LED neon signs?

Typical production lead time is 7–14 days depending on artwork complexity, size, quantity, and mounting requirement. Multi-site rollout programs are phased according to your schedule.

### Custom Planter Box

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-planter-box
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-planter-box/index.md

Architectural planter solutions that bring greenery into hotels, commercial entrances, and public spaces. Coordinate the shape, appearance, and project requirements directly with our factory team.

[GET A PROJECT QUOTE](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) Check Feasibility

What to send for a custom planter box project

- • Drawings or artwork
- • Dimensions and target quantity
- • Material, drainage and finish
- • Installation/site photos and ship-to country

Send what you have: artwork, approximate dimensions, quantity, finish or lighting direction, mounting/site photos, and ship-to country.

![Custom architectural planter boxes with greenery](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/custom-planter-box.jpg)

Planter boxes: the short answer

A fabricated planter box has to satisfy three things at once: it has to sit correctly against the building, it has to hold and drain the planting it was designed around, and it has to survive the exposure of the place it stands in. Form, body construction, drainage, and finish are therefore confirmed against the project drawings before production rather than chosen from a stock size.

#### How is a planter box coordinated with the building?

The visible faces are the part that matters. Profile, height, and edge detail are aligned to the paving, dado, or seating datum they stand against, so the planter reads as part of the architecture instead of an object placed in front of it. Where the brief contains enough information to prepare one, a 3D mockup is used to check scale and proportion before the body is drawn for production.

[See landscape furniture](https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-landscape-furniture)

#### Which materials suit planters that stay outdoors?

Bodies are commonly aluminum or galvanized steel, with stainless steel where the project specifies it. The surface finish is selected for the specified project environment, and the exposure of the actual location — coastal or salt-air conditions, de-icing practice, and how the planter is maintained — is confirmed per project rather than assumed. The material guide sets out how the exposed-metal options compare.

[Review material selection logic](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### How are drainage and planting handled inside the body?

An internal liner, a drainage outlet or perforation direction, and the interface with the irrigation and overflow arrangement are all part of the body rather than an afterthought. The planting type drives the root volume and soil load, and those in turn affect the body construction and the base detail. These items are confirmed with the landscape contractor and the project team before fabrication.

[Confirm drainage and base details](https://www.zydsign.com/contact)

#### Can a planter body carry brand identification?

Yes, and it is usually worth doing. A logo or brand panel applied to the visible face lets the planting read as part of the same identity programme as the building signage, with contrast and placement confirmed against the brand standard in the same way as a metal and acrylic logo sign. Graphic direction is agreed before the finish is applied, since the panel and the body are finished together.

[See logo signs](https://www.zydsign.com/products/metal-acrylic-logo-sign)

Medical signage: the short answer

Medical signage succeeds when a visitor can find the right department without asking for help and staff can update a room name without replacing the wall. The system combines clear directional panels with modular room and department identification, specified for the cleaning routine and mounting conditions of each care area.

#### How is a hospital wayfinding system organized?

Hospitals are usually planned as a hierarchy: campus arrival, building entry, vertical circulation, department entries, and finally room identification. Each level answers one decision, which keeps the panels simple and the visitor moving. The general selection guide explains how to match sign formats to the site and viewer.

#### Which materials and finishes suit healthcare interiors?

Panels are commonly aluminum or acrylic with printed or applied graphics, finished so the surface can be cleaned routinely without damaging the print. Edges and mounting are chosen to reduce ledges, and room plates are designed to be replaceable as departments change. The material guide covers the exposed-metal alternatives used outdoors.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What makes healthcare signage different from general commercial signage?

Healthcare signage has to work for people who are stressed, moving quickly, or unfamiliar with the building, so clarity, contrast, and consistent placement matter more than decoration. ##### Can signage be specified for hygienic healthcare environments?

Panels, edges, and graphics can be specified with surface finishes suited to routine cleaning, and mounting methods can be chosen to reduce ledges where dirt collects. Logo signs: the short answer

A cut metal and acrylic logo sign reproduces the brand mark as a physical, layered object rather than a flat print, which gives walls depth, shadow, and a premium finish. Choose it for reception and interior feature walls where the mark is seen close up, and in a suitable build for exterior plaques.

#### When should a brand choose a metal logo sign over printed graphics?

Choose fabricated metal when the logo is viewed at close range and the space calls for a tactile, dimensional finish: reception desks, boardroom walls, and flagship interiors. Printed graphics remain efficient for large-format or temporary use. Our selection guide explains how to match the sign format to the space and viewing distance.

[Read the sign-selection guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business)

#### Which finishes work for interior and exterior logo signs?

Interior marks often use brushed or mirror stainless, anodized-look aluminum, or powder-coated color with an acrylic face layer. Exterior plaques need a finish route suited to weather and cleaning, so the material choice follows the exposure. The outdoor material guide covers the stainless and coated-steel trade-offs.

[Review outdoor material options](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### What artwork is needed for a fabricated logo sign?

Vector artwork is the reliable starting point because the mark is cut and layered rather than printed, and very fine strokes may need adjustment for the material. Include the intended size, the wall surface, and any brand color references. The review confirms layer build-up and mounting before production.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What is the difference between a metal logo sign and a channel letter sign?

A metal and acrylic logo sign is usually a flat or layered plaque carrying the brand mark, often for a reception wall or boardroom. Channel letters are individual illuminated or non-illuminated letterforms built as separate volumes for larger identification. The two are frequently specified together for one brand.

##### Which materials are used for cut metal and acrylic logo signs?

Common routes are stainless steel, aluminum, or coated sheet for the metal layer, and acrylic for the face or the standoff layer. The finish is chosen to match the interior and the required appearance, from brushed metal to powder-coated color. The material guide compares the outdoor stainless and coated-steel routes.

### Outdoor Pylon & Monument Signs

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/products/outdoor-pylon-monument-sign

![Outdoor Pylon Monument Sign](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/cat-outdoor.webp)

Pylon vs monument: the short answer

Choose a pylon sign when the entry must be identified from a distance, above roadside obstacles, or across multiple approach lanes. Choose a monument sign when a lower, wider presence tied to the site and landscape suits the brand better. The decision follows the approach distance, permitted height, site context, and message hierarchy, not a fixed rule.

#### How are large pylon signs engineered for wind load?

Wind resistance is a site-specific engineering question, not a fixed specification. Our engineering team provides project-specific wind load calculations and foundation specifications when the site location, overall dimensions, and local conditions are confirmed. The illumination and power components are selected and reviewed against the confirmed exterior application.

[Read the sign-selection guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business)

#### Which materials should an outdoor monument sign use?

Material selection starts with the finish the brand needs, the exposure of the site, and how the structure will be fabricated and maintained. Common routes include galvanized sheet, 201 and 304 stainless steel, and aluminum plate, each followed by a specified coating or finish system. For a fuller comparison of stainless and coated-steel routes, review our material guide before sending a brief.

[Compare outdoor sign materials](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### What sizes can you manufacture?

Overall dimensions are confirmed against the project drawing, the viewing distance, and the site, so there is no responsible one-size answer. Share the approximate height and width, the approach distance, and any permitted-height constraint, and the engineering review will confirm the structural approach before production. Recent landmark projects give a practical sense of what the factory builds at scale.

[See landmark project references](https://www.zydsign.com/projects)

#### When does a pylon or monument sign need coordinated engineering?

Any tall or site-integrated structure benefits from an early engineering conversation: wind exposure, foundation or ground interface, power routing, service access, and local review requirements all belong in the brief. Projects that combine entry identity with wider wayfinding needs are often delivered together as one coordinated program.

[Explore wayfinding systems](https://www.zydsign.com/products/architectural-wayfinding-system)

A pylon sign is a tall, freestanding identification structure usually chosen when the sign must be read from a distance or above surrounding objects. ### Custom Outdoor Waste Bin

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/products/outdoor-waste-bin
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/products/outdoor-waste-bin/index.md

A refined waste bin solution for hotels, commercial spaces, and public environments. Coordinate the visible form, branding, and project requirements directly with our factory team.

What to send for a custom outdoor waste bin project

- • Dimensions, capacity and quantity

Send what you have: artwork, approximate dimensions, quantity, finish or lighting direction, mounting/site photos, and ship-to country.

![Custom outdoor waste bin with logo panel](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/outdoor-waste-bin.jpg)

Waste bins: the short answer

A public-realm waste bin is judged by two things that rarely appear on the drawing: whether the collection crew can service it quickly, and whether it still looks intact after a season of use. Planning therefore starts from the separation streams and the collection routine, and only then settles the shape of the body, the opening, and the fixing detail.

#### How are waste separation streams planned on site?

Most public programmes run at least a general-waste stream and a recyclable stream, grouped as stations at decision points rather than scattered as single units. The label or pictogram panel is treated as part of the site sign system so the waste graphics match the wayfinding language around them. The recycling stations installed in the Water Fashion Plaza walkways are an example of that grouping in use.

[See the installed recycling stations](https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/dalian-water-plaza-wayfinding-signage)

#### How is servicing access designed into the bin?

Opening direction, liner removal, and the clearance a crew needs to empty the unit decide whether a bin is actually used as intended; a unit that is awkward to service tends to be bypassed. The servicing method is confirmed with the operator and the maintenance team before the opening and liner details are frozen, so the daily task stays a one-person job.

[Confirm the servicing routine](https://www.zydsign.com/contact)

#### Which materials and finishes suit outdoor bins?

Bodies are commonly galvanized steel or aluminum, with stainless steel where the project specifies it, and the surface finish is selected for the specified project environment rather than for appearance alone. Edges and opening details are shaped so the body does not hold standing water, and the exposure of the actual location is confirmed per project. The material guide compares the exposed-metal options.

[Review material selection logic](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### How is a bin secured, and can it carry brand graphics?

Fixing is decided by the paving build-up, the wind exposure of the location, and whether the unit has to move for cleaning, so it is either surface-fixed or ballasted rather than simply set down. A logo or stream panel is applied to the body in the same way as a metal and acrylic logo sign, with placement and contrast confirmed against the brand standard before the finish goes on.

[See logo signs](https://www.zydsign.com/products/metal-acrylic-logo-sign)

#### Why an outdoor bin is a materials decision first

A public-space bin is handled daily and left outside permanently, so the body material and its finish decide how long the unit keeps its appearance. ##### Can bins be supplied for a multi-stream recycling programme?

### Portable Metal A-Frame Signs

![Portable metal A-frame sign](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/a-frame-sign.webp)

Portable metal A-frame signs: the short answer

#### A sign that stands on its own, wherever the customer is

A portable metal A-frame sign is a free-standing sign that carries its own frame and stands on the ground rather than on a wall. The A-frame shape presents a face on each side, so the message can be read from either direction of approach, and the whole unit can be lifted, moved, or brought in at the end of the day. That combination is what makes it the practical choice where the position that matters is on the pavement or the forecourt instead of the building itself. The build is settled against the artwork and the site it will stand on before production starts.

Typical Applications

#### Where an A-frame sign earns its place

The common thread is a spot that has to be signed but cannot be built on. A wall sign is fixed once and stays; an A-frame goes where the people are today and moves when they do.

01

##### Pavements & Shopfronts

Puts the offer on the pavement outside the door, where someone walking past is already looking.

02

##### Forecourts & Entrances

Directs traffic at a driveway, gate, or entrance that a wall sign cannot address from the street.

03

##### Events & Market Stands

Travels with the stand and folds away afterwards, which suits venues used for a day at a time.

04

##### Temporary Site Directions

Handles short-term wayfinding where the route changes and a fixed sign would misdirect.

Related Reading

#### Choosing the material for a sign that lives outdoors

A free-standing sign that stands on a pavement, forecourt or event floor is exposed to weather, handling and moving, so the material decision carries more weight than it does indoors. The comparison of [304 stainless steel and galvanized steel for outdoor signs](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs) sets out how the two routes differ by exposure, finish and fabrication.

Where the sign type is still open, the guide to [choosing the right sign for a business](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business) compares a portable sign against pylon, monument, building and wayfinding signage, and explains which of those a site actually needs.

Whichever route is chosen, the surface finish and the cleaning access are reviewed together, which is the approach described in the [materials and finishes guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/signage-material-selection-guide).

Questions

#### A-frame sign FAQs

##### What is a portable metal A-frame sign used for?

It is a free-standing sign that stands on the ground on its own frame rather than being fixed to a wall, which makes it the usual choice for a pavement, forecourt, entrance, or event stand where the sign has to come in at night or move between sites. Because it is not fixed, the same sign can be repositioned as the footfall or the layout of a site changes.

##### Does an A-frame sign show a message on both sides?

An A-frame presents a face on each side by definition, which is what lets it be read from either direction of approach. Whether the two faces carry the same artwork or two different messages is settled with the project.

##### How is an A-frame sign kept stable outdoors?

It is kept stable through the weight and the footprint of the frame itself, and where the site is exposed the build can be specified with additional ballast. How much, and in what form, depends on the site and is confirmed with the project rather than assumed.

##### What is the minimum order and lead time for an A-frame sign?

Minimum order is 1 unit and typical production lead time is 7–14 days depending on artwork, quantity, and finish. DDP delivery and any warranty terms are confirmed in the project quotation.

#### Planning an A-frame sign?

Send the artwork, the number of units, and the pavement or site the sign will stand on for a project-specific review.

### Ultra-Slim LED Light Boxes

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/products/ultra-slim-led-light-box

Edge-lit illuminated panels for retail fascias, transport interiors, and corporate lobbies.

What to send for an ultra-slim LED light box

- • Artwork or panel file
- • Panel dimensions and quantity
- • Finish, colour and lighting direction
- • Mounting/site photos and ship-to country

Send what you have: artwork, approximate dimensions, quantity, finish or lighting direction, mounting/site photos, and ship-to country.

![Ultra-Slim LED Light Box](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/cat-lightbox.jpg)

Ultra-slim light boxes: the short answer

An ultra-slim light box lights a printed or translucent graphic from its edges rather than from modules behind the panel, which keeps the profile shallow and the face evenly lit. Choose this format when mounting depth is limited or when a clean, close-to-the-wall illuminated panel fits the space better than a deep cabinet.

#### When should a project choose an edge-lit light box?

Edge-lit panels suit shallow fascias, framed wall recesses, menu and directory boards, and interior applications where depth is limited. Where very large panels or high brightness are required, a different construction may serve the site better. Sharing the panel size and mounting depth lets the correct build be confirmed.

[Read the sign-selection guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/how-to-choose-the-right-sign-for-your-business)

#### Which graphics and materials work best in a light box?

The graphic has to transmit light evenly, so the substrate and print method are chosen together with the panel. Metal or coated frames handle exposed locations, while acrylic faces are common for interior applications. The material guide explains how the finish route affects durability outdoors.

[Review outdoor material options](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs)

#### What information is needed for a light box quotation?

Send the panel dimensions, quantity, artwork, mounting surface and depth, indoor or outdoor exposure, and the required finish. Where the box replaces an existing unit, a photo and the fixing layout speed up the review. Those details make the quotation comparable and the installation plan reliable.

[Send your project brief](https://www.zydsign.com/contact)

#### How does a light box fit into a wider signage program?

Illuminated panels often work alongside dimensional letters, wayfinding, or entry monuments, sharing the same lighting temperature and finish so the brand reads consistently. Coordinating them in one order keeps components matched and simplifies installation on site.

[See matching dimensional letters](https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-halo-lit-letters)

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What makes a light box "ultra-slim"?

The profile depth comes from edge-lighting the graphic panel instead of placing modules behind it. A slimmer box suits shallow fascias, framed walls, and interior applications where a deep cabinet would sit proud of the surface. The achievable depth depends on the panel size and the required brightness.

##### Can an ultra-slim light box be used outdoors?

Yes, provided the construction and sealing are specified for the location. Outdoor installations need an enclosure and power route suited to rain, wind, and temperature movement, while interior boxes can use lighter construction. Confirm the mounting surface and exposure with the brief so the right build is quoted.

### 304 Stainless Steel vs Galvanized Steel for Outdoor Signs

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/guides/304-stainless-steel-vs-galvanized-steel-outdoor-signs/index.md

A buyer-focused way to compare two common material routes for outdoor signage before requesting drawings, finish samples, and a project quotation.

Guide • Updated Sep 7, 2026 • By Aaron, ZYD Signage

304 stainless steel is a strong starting point when an outdoor sign needs a stainless appearance and the exposure, finish, fabrication, and maintenance plan support it. Galvanized steel can be a practical route for painted sign structures when the coating system and site conditions are properly specified. The right choice depends on the project brief, not on a universal “best” material.

#### Which material fits your outdoor sign brief?

Start with the sign's role, exposure, appearance, accessibility requirements, fabrication details, and maintenance access. Then ask the supplier to show the proposed layer build-up and finish in writing. For ZYD, the procurement conversation should begin with the site location, sign type, approximate dimensions, lighting requirement, quantity, installation responsibility, and destination so the material recommendation can be checked against the actual project.

#### 304 Stainless Steel vs Galvanized Steel: the short answer

| Decision factor | 304 stainless steel | Galvanized steel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visual brief | Useful where a brushed, polished, or exposed stainless appearance is part of the design brief. | Usually paired with a specified paint or powder-coat finish when the structure is intended to be coated. |
| Exposure question | Still requires review of pollutants, salt exposure, crevices, finish, drainage, and cleaning access. | Requires review of the zinc protection, cut edges, joints, coating system, drainage, and planned maintenance. |
| Fabrication | Welding, grinding, brushing, polishing, and contamination control should be agreed before production. | Fabrication sequence and post-fabrication protection should be defined so exposed areas receive the intended protection. |
| Best procurement next step | Request a finish sample, edge/joint detail, cleaning note, and site-exposure review. | Request the complete protection and paint specification, including touch-up and installation coordination. |

#### What should a buyer confirm before choosing?

##### 1. Where will the sign be installed?

Record whether the sign is indoors, in a normal outdoor environment, near a coast, beside a road, in an industrial area, or in a location where cleaning access is limited. These are procurement inputs, not proof that one grade is suitable in every site.

##### 2. Is the finish part of the brand experience?

A stainless face may be selected for its visual texture, while a galvanized steel structure may be selected for a coated architectural finish. Ask for a sample or approved finish reference rather than relying on a material name alone.

##### 3. How will accessibility be coordinated?

Material selection does not decide accessibility compliance. Confirm the sign type, tactile or raised content where applicable, character layout, mounting position, contrast, and local approval path with the project designer and the authority having jurisdiction. Use the U.S. Access Board references below when the project falls under that framework; do not treat this guide as legal advice.

##### 4. What must appear in the quotation?

Ask the supplier to separate face material, internal frame, finish, illumination, mounting hardware, packing, shipping scope, installation responsibility, drawings, and maintenance notes. This makes two material proposals easier to compare without assuming unverified specifications.

#### ZYD procurement checklist

This is ZYD's practical request list for preparing a project review. It is a procurement workflow, not a claim that either material is automatically compliant or suitable.

- • Site city/country and exposure notes, including coastal or industrial conditions.
- • Sign type: pylon sign, monument sign, directional sign, building sign, or another defined type.
- • Approximate dimensions, quantity, artwork, illumination, and viewing direction.
- • Required appearance: exposed stainless finish, painted finish, or a finish sample for approval.
- • Installation location, access constraints, foundation/interface responsibility, and local review requirements.
- • Destination and delivery scope, so packaging and shipping can be discussed with the actual project brief.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### Which material is better for an outdoor sign?

Neither material is automatically better for every site. Compare the exposure, appearance, finish, fabrication, drainage, cleaning access, maintenance plan, and local project requirements before selecting 304 stainless steel or galvanized steel.

##### Is 304 stainless steel maintenance-free outdoors?

Do not treat 304 stainless steel as maintenance-free. Site exposure, finish, crevices, contamination, drainage, and cleaning access still need review, especially near coastal or industrial environments.

##### What should be included in a material comparison quotation?

Ask for the face and structural materials, finish system, edge and joint details, mounting hardware, drawings, packing, shipping scope, installation responsibility, and maintenance notes so both proposals describe a comparable scope.

#### Sources & further reading

The links below are public references used for terminology, accessibility context, and stainless-steel selection background. They are not ZYD product claims. Project compliance remains the responsibility of the design team and the authority having jurisdiction.

1. International Sign Association (ISA) — Glossary of Sign Terms and Definitions Terminology reference for sign types and project language.
2. U.S. Access Board — Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Official accessibility reference; confirm the applicable jurisdiction and project code path.
3. U.S. Access Board — Chapter 7: Signs Official signs guidance for accessibility planning; it is not a substitute for the authority having jurisdiction.
4. International Molybdenum Association — Which Stainless Steel? Public technical guidance for thinking about stainless-steel selection and exposure.
5. Nickel Institute — Design Guidelines for the Selection and Use of Stainless Steels Public technical handbook for material-selection context and design considerations.

#### Send the project inputs

Share the site, sign type, approximate dimensions, finish preference, quantity, and destination. ZYD can review the brief before recommending a fabrication route.
