### Trimless vs. Trim Cap Channel Letters: Construction, Appearance and Maintenance

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/guides/trimless-vs-trim-cap-channel-letters
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/guides/trimless-vs-trim-cap-channel-letters/index.md

How trimless and trim cap channel letters differ in face attachment, edge appearance, logo detail, servicing and outdoor specification.

Guide • Updated Oct 19, 2026 • By Aaron, ZYD Signage

Trimless channel letters have no visible trim cap around the illuminated face. Trim cap channel letters use a visible perimeter trim to retain the face. Both can produce effective illuminated signs, but they differ in edge appearance, face attachment and servicing arrangements.

#### A Note on Terminology

Sign-making terminology varies between suppliers and markets.

In this article, trim cap channel letters means letters with a visible retaining trim around the face. Some suppliers use “rimmed letters” more broadly to describe other metal-edge constructions.

Similarly, trimless describes the absence of a visible face trim cap. It does not mean the letter has no sidewalls, internal supports or face-retaining components. Ask for a face-edge detail or cross-sectional drawing before comparing quotations.

#### Trimless and Trim Cap Letters at a Glance

![Two illuminated letter A signs photographed side by side, labelled TRIMLESS on the left and TRIM CAP on the right](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/trimless-vs-trim-cap-faces-side-by-side.jpg)

For buyers, the decision involves more than choosing a cleaner-looking edge. Letter size, logo detail, installation conditions and access for repairs should also be considered.

| Feature | Trimless Channel Letters | Trim Cap Channel Letters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Face perimeter | No visible trim cap | Visible retaining trim around the face |
| Typical appearance | Uninterrupted illuminated face | Defined border framing the illuminated face |
| Face attachment | Depends on the manufacturer’s construction | Face commonly assembled with a perimeter trim cap |
| Visual considerations | Face alignment and edge finishing | Trim width, color and corner detailing |
| Service access | Must be confirmed for the proposed design | Must be confirmed for the proposed design |
| Main purchasing question | How is the face secured and replaced? | How is the trimmed face assembly secured and removed? |

#### 1. How Are Trim Cap Channel Letters Constructed?

![Close-up edge detail comparing a trimless letter face labelled NO VISIBLE FACE TRIM with a trim cap face labelled VISIBLE RETAINING TRIM](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/trimless-vs-trim-cap-edge-detail.jpg)

A typical front-lit trim cap letter includes a translucent face, a perimeter trim cap, fabricated sidewalls, a back and internal LEDs.

The trim cap surrounds the face and connects it to the letter body through the specified fastening arrangement. Depending on the system, the trim may be made from plastic or another suitable material. From the front, the trim creates a visible outline around the illuminated area.

Confirm the trim material, color, width and fastening method. Review tight curves, sharp corners and small internal openings, where the trim can have a noticeable effect on the final appearance. Ask whether the face assembly can be removed on site and what tools or access are required.

#### 2. How Are Trimless Channel Letters Constructed?

Trimless letters remove the visible face trim cap, creating a cleaner transition between the illuminated face and the sidewall.

The face may be retained through a recessed arrangement, internal components, bonding or another engineered assembly. The exact method varies between manufacturers and letter designs. Some constructions use a machined acrylic face with a shaped edge; others use a different interface between the face and letter body.

A product description that says only “trimless” does not fully explain the structure.

- • The acrylic face and its edge profile.
- • The connection between the face and sidewalls.
- • Any internal retaining components.
- • The fastening or bonding method.
- • The intended service-access route.

#### 3. How Does the Appearance Differ?

![Four-panel comparison of trimless and trim cap letters shown in daylight and at night](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/trimless-vs-trim-cap-day-and-night-comparison.jpg)

Without a visible trim cap, the illuminated face can appear more continuous. This may suit simple logos, contemporary storefronts and designs where the face-edge detail is particularly visible. The result depends on fabrication quality: uneven face alignment, inconsistent joints or visible adhesive can weaken the intended effect.

Trim cap letters have a deliberate border around the face. The border can match the sidewall, coordinate with the brand or create contrast. Its visual impact depends on the letter size and viewing distance. On small letters or narrow strokes, the trim may occupy a substantial part of the visible face. On larger letters viewed from farther away, the difference may be less noticeable.

For a useful comparison, request both options using the same artwork, dimensions, face color and lighting conditions. Comparing unrelated logos or differently exposed photographs can make one construction appear better for reasons unrelated to the trim.

#### 4. Which Works Better for Detailed Logos?

![Close-up of the counter inside a letter R, comparing trimless and trim cap face edges](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/trimless-vs-trim-cap-counter-detail-r.jpg)

Neither construction automatically reproduces every logo accurately. Thin strokes, small counters, acute corners and closely spaced elements can limit fabrication and LED placement.

With trim cap letters, the perimeter trim needs to follow the shape while leaving sufficient illuminated face area. With trimless letters, the face-retaining method and sidewall construction also require adequate space.

Ask the manufacturer to identify any proposed artwork adjustments before production. Review those changes against the original logo rather than allowing unapproved simplification.

#### 5. Does Trimless Mean Brighter?

No. Removing the trim cap does not automatically make a sign brighter or more evenly illuminated. Light output and uniformity depend on the complete design, including LED arrangement and output, letter depth, face material and light transmission, stroke width and internal geometry, printed graphics or applied films, and the power supply specification.

Trimless construction changes the visible edge, but lighting performance still needs to be checked through a representative working sample. For both types, inspect narrow strokes, corners and transitions between large and small illuminated areas.

- • LED arrangement and output.
- • Letter depth.
- • Face material and light transmission.
- • Stroke width and internal geometry.
- • Printed graphics or applied films.
- • Power supply specification.

#### 6. What Are the Maintenance Differences?

![Letter shell opened to show internal LEDs, a removable face panel and a screwdriver used for servicing](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/trimless-vs-trim-cap-service-panel-and-leds.jpg)

The most useful maintenance question is: how will this particular letter be opened, repaired and reassembled?

Some trim cap systems allow the trimmed face assembly to be removed from the front. This can provide access to internal components when the design and installation permit it. Confirm the fastener positions, removal procedure and whether the trim can be reused after servicing. A visible trim cap alone does not guarantee convenient access.

Trimless systems vary considerably. Some provide a removable face or another planned access route. Other constructions may require the letter to be removed from the wall or a bonded component to be replaced. Ask for the servicing procedure before approval: a clean front appearance should be supported by a practical maintenance plan.

Access can also be affected by the mounting height, wall arrangement, cable routing and power supply location. Even a serviceable letter can be difficult to maintain if the power supply is concealed in an inaccessible space.

#### 7. Which Is Better for Outdoor Use?

Either construction may be specified for outdoor applications when the complete sign is designed for the intended environment. The presence or absence of a trim cap does not establish weather resistance.

Discuss exposure to rain and wind-driven moisture, joints, seals and drainage arrangements, temperature conditions, face-retention design, material and finish suitability, electrical connections and power supply location, and local installation requirements with the manufacturer.

Request evidence relevant to the proposed assembly where required. Do not assume that a rating associated with one component applies to the entire installed sign.

#### 8. How Do Costs Compare?

Trimless letters are not always more expensive, and trim cap letters are not always the lower-cost option. Pricing depends on the letter dimensions, quantity, materials, face machining, assembly method, finish and production complexity.

A simple trimless design produced with an established system may be economical. A complex trim cap logo with many tight curves may require substantial labor. Compare quotations using an agreed specification rather than construction names alone.

| Quotation item | What to confirm |
| --- | --- |
| Artwork | Same logo, dimensions and approved adjustments |
| Face | Material, thickness, color and decoration |
| Sidewalls | Material, depth and finish |
| Face attachment | Retaining method and relevant components |
| Lighting | LED specification and proposed arrangement |
| Maintenance | Access and replacement procedure |
| Installation | Fixings, wiring and positioning template |
| Delivery | Protective packaging and supplied components |

#### 9. How to Approve a Sample

![Removable face panel and internal LED layout used to demonstrate how a channel letter is serviced](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/trimless-vs-trim-cap-service-panel-and-leds.jpg)

A useful sample should represent the proposed production construction. Choose a letter or logo section containing a challenging feature, such as a narrow stroke, internal opening or tight corner.

Inspect it with the lights switched off and on. During the daytime check, review face alignment, joints, trim consistency, paint finish and visible fasteners. During the illuminated check, review brightness consistency, unwanted edge light and dark areas.

Finally, ask the supplier to demonstrate how the sample would be serviced. This connects the approved appearance with the actual construction.

#### Trimless or trim cap: what to confirm

Both constructions can work. The quotation should describe how the face is held, how it is serviced and how the installed sign is expected to perform.

- • Face-edge detail or cross-section drawing.
- • Trim material, color, width and fastening method (trim cap).
- • Face retention, bonding and internal supports (trimless).
- • Proposed artwork adjustments at small counters and tight corners.
- • Lighting sample checked at the intended size and depth.
- • Removal and reassembly procedure for the specific design.
- • Outdoor joints, seals, drainage and power supply location.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What is the main difference between trimless and trim cap channel letters?

Trimless letters have no visible retaining trim cap around the face. Trim cap letters have a visible perimeter trim. The face attachment and servicing method depend on the specific construction.

##### Do trimless letters have metal sides?

They can. “Trimless” refers to the face-edge appearance, not the absence of sidewalls. Confirm the sidewall material in the specification.

##### Are trimless letters the same as edge-lit letters?

No. Trimless describes a construction detail. Edge-lit describes a lighting method. The terms should not be treated as interchangeable.

##### Are trim cap letters easier to repair?

Some systems offer convenient front access, but this should be verified. Compare the actual removal and replacement procedures for both proposed options.

##### Can either construction use UV-printed faces?

UV-printed decoration can be specified where compatible with the face material and design. Approve the daytime color and illuminated appearance because printing can affect light transmission.

##### Which option should I choose for my storefront?

Compare both using your actual logo, intended dimensions and viewing conditions. Choose the construction that provides the required appearance, reliable fabrication and a workable maintenance arrangement.

#### Sources & further reading

These public references support terminology, accessibility context, or material-selection background. They are not ZYD product claims; project compliance and final specifications must be confirmed with the design team and the authority having jurisdiction.

1. International Sign Association (ISA) — Glossary of Sign Terms and Definitions Public terminology reference for sign construction and lighting discussions.

[See custom front-lit channel letters](https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-channel-letters) [See custom halo-lit letters](https://www.zydsign.com/products/custom-halo-lit-letters) [Compare front-lit and halo-lit channel letters](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/front-lit-vs-halo-lit-channel-letters) [Read the illuminated signage buying guide](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/illuminated-signage-buying-guide) [Signage glossary](https://www.zydsign.com/guides/signage-glossary) [Discuss trimless and trim cap options](https://www.zydsign.com/contact) Get Material Advice

Buyer brief

#### Ask for the face-edge detail

Send the vector artwork, required dimensions and photographs of the installation surface, and ask for a face-edge detail or cross-section for each option. That drawing explains more than the construction name.

### What Does IP65 Mean for Outdoor Channel Letters? Protection Ratings and Installation Conditions

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/guides/what-does-ip65-mean-outdoor-channel-letters
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/guides/what-does-ip65-mean-outdoor-channel-letters/index.md

How to interpret IP65 for outdoor channel letters, distinguish component ratings from complete-sign protection, and specify installation conditions, evidence and limitations.

Guide • Updated Oct 22, 2026 • By Aaron, ZYD Signage

IP65 means an enclosure is dust-tight and protected against water jets under specified test conditions. It does not mean a sign is suitable for immersion, pressure washing or every outdoor environment. An IP rating for an LED module or power supply does not automatically apply to the complete sign.

#### 1. What Does IP65 Stand For?

![IP65 overview showing a dust-covered and water-sprayed enclosure labelled dust-tight and water jets](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/what-does-ip65-mean-outdoor-channel-letters-overview.jpg)

IP refers to ingress protection. The IP code defined in IEC 60529 describes protection provided by an enclosure.

The two numbers address different types of ingress:

| Part of the Code | Meaning | Practical Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | Dust-tight | No ingress of dust under the specified test conditions |
| 5 | Protection against water jets | Water jets directed at the enclosure must not cause harmful effects under the specified test conditions |

These are defined test classifications, rather than a general promise that a product is “completely waterproof.”

The rating should be read alongside the product documentation and installation instructions.

#### 2. Does IP65 Mean an Illuminated Sign Can Be Used Outdoors?

IP65 can be relevant to outdoor use, but the rating alone does not establish complete outdoor suitability.

An outdoor sign may also face sunlight, salt deposits, temperature changes, condensation, wind and cleaning chemicals. These conditions require separate consideration.

For example, a rated enclosure may resist the specified water-jet test while its decorative finish is unsuitable for prolonged coastal exposure.

Likewise, a protected power supply still needs to operate within its specified temperature and installation limits.

Evaluate the complete sign against its location rather than selecting it by an IP number alone.

#### 3. Component Ratings and Complete-Sign Ratings Are Different

![LED module, power supply and complete channel letter illustrating that component ratings are not whole-sign ratings](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/what-does-ip65-mean-outdoor-channel-letters-component-vs-sign.jpg)

An illuminated sign contains multiple components and interfaces.

These may include:

- • LED modules.
- • Power supplies.
- • Connectors and cable joints.
- • Junction boxes.
- • Cable-entry fittings.
- • Letter faces, returns and backs.
- • Service covers and fastening points.

##### An IP67 LED Module Does Not Make the Letter IP67

The module’s rating applies to that module in its specified configuration. It does not establish the protection of the surrounding letter enclosure or its wiring connections.

##### An IP65 Power Supply Does Not Rate the Whole Installation

The power supply’s documentation does not automatically cover field-made cable joints, nearby junction boxes or modified cable entries.

##### A Drained Letter Is Not Necessarily a Dust-Tight Enclosure

Some outdoor channel letters use drainage openings as part of their construction.

That can be a deliberate design approach, but a drained housing should not be described as a dust-tight IP65 enclosure without evidence supporting that classification.

Ask whether the stated rating applies to the complete letter, its internal components or another defined part of the system.

#### 4. IP65, IP66 and IP67: What Is the Difference?

Do not interpret these as a simple ranking in which every higher number automatically covers every lower-numbered water test.

Jet exposure and immersion are different conditions. Where both are relevant, request evidence for both rather than assuming an immersion rating establishes resistance to water jets.

Also confirm the scope of any rating: the LED module, power supply or complete enclosure.

| Rating | Dust Protection | Water Protection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IP65 | Dust-tight | Water jets |
| IP66 | Dust-tight | Powerful water jets |
| IP67 | Dust-tight | Temporary immersion under specified conditions |

#### 5. What Does IP65 Not Establish?

![Examples of conditions not established by IP65 including UV, corrosion, condensation and pressure-washer suitability](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/what-does-ip65-mean-outdoor-channel-letters-not-established.jpg)

An IP65 claim addresses defined ingress tests. It does not establish every property required for an outdoor sign.

##### Pressure-Washer Suitability

IP65 does not authorize unrestricted pressure washing.

Cleaning pressure, nozzle distance, water temperature and chemicals may differ substantially from the rating’s test conditions.

Follow the supplied cleaning instructions.

##### Resistance to Condensation

Moisture can form inside an assembly when temperature and humidity conditions change.

An ingress rating is not a guarantee against internal condensation. The design may need an appropriate moisture-management strategy.

##### Corrosion Resistance

IP65 does not specify resistance to salt, industrial pollutants or corrosion.

Base-metal selection, surface treatment, fasteners and maintenance remain important.

##### UV and Color Stability

The rating does not establish how acrylic, paint, cable insulation or seals will age in sunlight.

##### Mechanical Strength

Wind loads, impact resistance and fixing strength are separate matters.

##### Complete Electrical Approval

An IP rating is not a substitute for the electrical safety assessment, labeling or local approval required for the project.

#### 6. Match the Sign to the Installation Environment

![Channel letter installation examples in sheltered, exposed and coastal environments](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/what-does-ip65-mean-outdoor-channel-letters-environment.jpg)

The installation environment determines which parts of the sign and its documentation need closer review.

##### Sheltered Storefronts

A canopy can reduce direct rain exposure, but the sign may still encounter wind-driven water, condensation and cleaning spray.

Describe the actual conditions rather than classifying the location simply as “covered.”

##### Fully Exposed Facades

Review the complete assembly, including cable entries, joints, covers and equipment locations.

Confirm the permitted mounting orientation. A configuration assessed in one orientation should not automatically be assumed suitable in another.

##### Coastal Locations

Salt exposure requires more than an ingress rating.

Discuss the metal grade, coating system, connectors, fasteners and cleaning access. Include the actual location and exposure conditions in the specification.

##### Cold Climates

Confirm operating-temperature limits for LEDs, power supplies and other components.

Snow, ice, moisture and freeze-thaw conditions may require additional design review. IP65 alone does not address them.

##### Areas Subject to Frequent Washing

Provide the cleaning method, chemicals, water temperature and pressure.

Do not choose equipment solely because its description includes the word “waterproof.”

#### 7. Installation Details Can Change Protection

![Cable entries, sealed connections and power supply location details for an outdoor sign installation](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/guides/what-does-ip65-mean-outdoor-channel-letters-installation.jpg)

The performance of a rated product depends on maintaining its specified configuration.

##### Cable Entries

Use fittings compatible with the cable and enclosure. Follow the relevant instructions for assembly and sealing.

An unsuitable cable-entry opening can compromise an otherwise protected enclosure.

##### Connectors and Junctions

Protect the actual connection, not just the cable.

Where a connector has a rating, confirm the conditions under which it applies, including whether it must be fully mated and correctly assembled.

##### Power Supply Position

Confirm that the location, orientation, temperature and access arrangements match the manufacturer’s instructions.

Avoid locations where equipment could sit in accumulating water unless expressly designed for that condition.

##### Site Modifications

Additional holes, changed covers or altered seals may affect protection.

Coordinate modifications with the manufacturer rather than assuming the original rating remains applicable.

##### Drainage and Ventilation

Preserve any designed drainage or ventilation features.

Adding sealant everywhere may obstruct drainage or interfere with the intended construction. Follow the approved details rather than treating more sealant as an automatic improvement.

#### 8. What Evidence Should Buyers Request?

A useful IP claim should identify the product and the supporting documentation.

Ask for:

| Item | What to Check |
| --- | --- |
| Rated product | Exact component, enclosure or sign assembly |
| Model or configuration | Whether it matches the proposed supply |
| Standard | Applicable test standard and edition |
| Evidence | Relevant test report, certification record or documented manufacturer rating |
| Installation conditions | Orientation, fittings, covers and assembly requirements |
| Limitations | Exposure or operating conditions outside the stated scope |

A photograph of an LED module marked IP67 is not evidence that a fabricated sign is IP67.

For custom letters, ask whether the evidence covers the proposed construction or a defined product family. Clarify any differences before production.

#### 9. How Should Outdoor Protection Be Written into a Quotation?

Avoid a specification that says only “IP65 waterproof letters.”

Instead, ask the quotation to identify:

- • 1. The scope of each IP claim.
- • 2. LED module and power supply models.
- • 3. Connector and cable-joint arrangements.
- • 4. Letter-enclosure construction.
- • 5. Cable-entry details.
- • 6. Drainage or moisture-management provisions.
- • 7. Mounting orientation and equipment location.
- • 8. Installation and cleaning instructions.
- • 9. Supporting documents.
- • 10. Warranty conditions.

Where the complete letter enclosure has not been rated, describe its outdoor construction and component ratings accurately rather than assigning an unsupported whole-sign rating.

#### Discuss Outdoor Sign Protection with ZYD SIGN

Dalian ZhiYuDao Signage & Tech. Co.Ltd — ZYD SIGN manufactures custom front-lit letters, halo-lit letters and illuminated logo signs.

Send your artwork, dimensions and installation photographs, together with the expected environmental conditions. Identify any required IP rating and whether it must apply to individual components or the complete sign enclosure.

Contact ZYD SIGN to discuss outdoor sign construction, electrical components and the documentation required for your project.

#### IP protection checks before ordering

Use this checklist to confirm that an IP claim describes the actual supplied configuration and installation conditions.

- • The exact rated component, enclosure or complete sign assembly is identified.
- • The stated IP rating is tied to a model or defined configuration.
- • LED modules, power supplies, connectors and cable joints are considered separately.
- • The mounting orientation and equipment location are documented.
- • Cable entries, junctions, covers and fastening points follow the specified details.
- • Drainage and ventilation features are preserved where the design requires them.
- • The installation environment includes rain, washing, coastal, cold and condensation conditions where relevant.
- • Cleaning pressure, nozzle distance, chemicals and water temperature are defined when washing is expected.
- • Supporting test, certification or manufacturer documentation is requested.
- • The quotation describes component ratings and whole-sign construction without unsupported guarantees.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### Is IP65 waterproof?

IP65 describes dust-tight protection and resistance to specified water jets. “Waterproof” without those limits can be misleading. IP65 does not establish immersion or unrestricted pressure-washing suitability.

##### Are IP65 channel letters suitable for rain?

They may be suitable for the intended installation, but verify the rated assembly, installation instructions and actual exposure. Rain suitability should not be inferred from an unrelated component rating.

##### Is IP67 always better than IP65?

Not for every exposure. IP67 addresses temporary immersion, while IP65 addresses water jets. Confirm the tests relevant to the application.

##### Do outdoor channel letters need a sealed housing?

Not every outdoor sign uses the same construction. Some use protected components within a drained housing. The design and protection claims should accurately describe the supplied system.

##### Can I seal all the drainage holes?

Do not alter designed drainage without the manufacturer’s approval. Blocking it may cause water to accumulate.

##### Does IP65 prevent corrosion?

No. Corrosion resistance depends on materials, finishes, exposure and maintenance.

##### Does an IP65 power supply make the complete sign IP65?

No. Its rating applies to the specified power supply configuration. The complete sign and field connections require separate consideration.

##### What information should I provide when ordering?

Share the installation location, exposure to rain and washing, temperature conditions, coastal conditions where relevant, mounting arrangement and any specified protection or approval requirements.

#### Sources & further reading

These public references support terminology, accessibility context, or material-selection background. They are not ZYD product claims; project compliance and final specifications must be confirmed with the design team and the authority having jurisdiction.

Buyer brief

#### Specify the complete installation

Share the sign location, exposure to rain or washing, temperature conditions, mounting arrangement and the exact component or enclosure to which any requested IP rating should apply.

## Case studies

### Water Fashion Plaza: Wayfinding and Signage in Dalian

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/dalian-water-plaza-wayfinding-signage
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/dalian-water-plaza-wayfinding-signage/index.md

A commercial complex in Dalian, China, needed one identification and wayfinding package that would hold together from the road outside to the third-floor corridor. ZYD Signage designed, manufactured and installed it.

Commercial Complex • Dalian, China • Wayfinding & Signage

![Illuminated green channel letters spelling the Water Fashion Plaza name on the building facade at night](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-facade-letters.jpg)

*Illuminated channel letters carrying the plaza name on the building facade.*

ZYD Signage delivered the complete wayfinding and signage system for Water Fashion Plaza, a commercial complex in Dalian, China. The package covers the outdoor illuminated building letters, a custom pylon sign that doubles as a tenant display, the garage entrance signage, interior directional signs and floor directories, functional space signage, and brand extension elements — all held together by the plaza brand green.

#### Project facts

#### Project background and the challenge

Water Fashion Plaza is a commercial complex in Dalian, China. A shopping centre of this scale has to answer several wayfinding questions in sequence: how visitors recognise the building from the road, how they read the tenant mix before they commit to parking, how they move through the garage, how they orient themselves once inside, and how they find everyday facilities such as restrooms, lifts and the information desk.

The signs also carry the identity of the complex itself. If the outdoor letters, the parking entrance, the floor directories and the room signs are designed independently, a visitor meets a different visual language at every step. The brief here was to hold one identity across the whole journey, indoors and out.

- One identification and wayfinding package for the approach, the garage, the concourse and the upper floors.
- The plaza brand green carried through every touchpoint rather than used as an outdoor accent only.
- A tenant display that tells visitors what is inside the complex before they enter.
- Facility signs that stay legible at a glance and match the rest of the system.

![Night view of the Water Fashion Plaza corner in Dalian with the illuminated building sign and lit storefronts](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-mall-exterior-night.jpg)

*Night view of the Water Fashion Plaza corner in Dalian with the illuminated building sign and lit storefronts*

#### The design language

The plaza brand green is the constant across the package. It appears on the outdoor illuminated letters, on the directional and directory graphics inside, on the facility signs and on the site furniture, so a visitor reads the same colour whether they are on the road outside or standing in a corridor upstairs.

Indoors the green works against white grounds rather than filling the whole face. The directory and directional signs use a light background with green accents, which keeps the tenant lists and the room names readable at a distance while still tying the sign back to the brand.

#### Outdoor main identity and the pylon sign

The primary identity element is the set of large illuminated letters mounted on the building facade, run in the plaza brand green so the complex reads as one object from a distance.

A custom pylon sign stands separately at the site. It is not only a name board: the same structure carries the plaza logo, an illuminated display of the resident brands and the wayfinding graphics, so it works as an identity marker and as a directory at the same time.

The facade also carries a large illuminated tenant brand wall, which turns the building elevation itself into part of the signage package rather than leaving it as plain cladding.

![Freestanding pylon sign at Water Fashion Plaza with the plaza logo, illuminated tenant panels and wayfinding graphics](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-pylon-sign.jpg)

*Freestanding pylon sign at Water Fashion Plaza with the plaza logo, illuminated tenant panels and wayfinding graphics*

![Illuminated tenant brand wall on the Water Fashion Plaza building facade at night](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-tenant-brand-wall.jpg)

*Illuminated tenant brand wall on the Water Fashion Plaza building facade at night*

#### Garage entrance signage

The garage entrance is treated as a single assembly instead of a row of unrelated panels. Entrance identification, the plaza logo and the regulatory markings a driver has to read at that exact moment are brought onto one unit: the height restriction, the speed limit and the no-horn requirement.

Reading them together matters because a driver meets all of these while moving. Separating the entrance name from the clearance marking would split one decision across two places the driver passes at speed.

![Garage entrance signage at Water Fashion Plaza combining the exit sign, plaza logo, height limit, speed limit and no-horn markings](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-garage-entrance-signage.jpg)

*Garage entrance signage at Water Fashion Plaza combining the exit sign, plaza logo, height limit, speed limit and no-horn markings*

#### Interior wayfinding and directories

Inside, suspended directional signs sit at the decision points where a visitor has to choose a direction. They use green arrows on light faces so the direction reads before the text does.

Free-standing floor directory totems carry the tenant lists for each level. They use white grounds with brand green accents, and they include a panel for current activity notices, so the directory can be updated with what is happening in the complex instead of only naming the tenants.

![Suspended interior directional sign with green arrows guiding visitors to the second floor facilities](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-overhead-wayfinding.jpg)

*Suspended interior directional sign with green arrows guiding visitors to the second floor facilities*

![Free-standing floor directory totems with white grounds and green accents in the Water Fashion Plaza concourse](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-floor-directory.jpg)

*Free-standing floor directory totems with white grounds and green accents in the Water Fashion Plaza concourse*

#### Functional space signage

Restrooms, lifts and the customer service desk use the same visual language as the wayfinding signs rather than a separate set of utility labels. The restroom identification is built as a cut-out profile mounted on a light wall, with a green directional arrow, so the family of symbols reads consistently beside the lift lobby.

The information desk carries the plaza identity into the interior fit-out. The counter is kept plain and the illuminated logo sign above it does the identifying, which keeps the desk legible without turning it into a billboard.

![Restroom identification with cut-out figures and a green directional arrow beside a lift lobby](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-restroom-signage.jpg)

*Restroom identification with cut-out figures and a green directional arrow beside a lift lobby*

![Information desk at Water Fashion Plaza with illuminated logo signage above the counter](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-information-desk.jpg)

*Information desk at Water Fashion Plaza with illuminated logo signage above the counter*

#### Brand extension and site furniture

The identity extends past the signs themselves. Illuminated logo work on the building and above the information desk, plus site furniture such as the segregated recycling stations, carry the same light finish and green iconography as the wayfinding package.

Treating furniture as part of the system is what stops a scheme from fragmenting: a visitor who has read green on the pylon, on a directional sign and on a room sign sees the same treatment again on the units in the walkway.

![Segregated recycling station units with green recycling symbols in a Water Fashion Plaza walkway](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dalian-water-plaza-recycling-station.jpg)

*Segregated recycling station units with green recycling symbols in a Water Fashion Plaza walkway*

#### Production, installation and quality control

The fabricated elements are built from stainless steel and acrylic. The production route covers laser cutting, seamless welding, powder coating and illuminated fabrication, which is what allows the outdoor letters, the pylon and the illuminated panels to be built to the same finish standard as the interior signs.

The service scope runs end to end rather than stopping at handover of the goods: design development, production, on-site installation and commissioning, followed by periodic maintenance. Work of this kind is manufactured at ZYD Signage in Dalian, a factory-direct operation established in 2006, and shipped to project sites.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What did ZYD Signage supply for Water Fashion Plaza?

The full wayfinding and signage package for the complex: the outdoor illuminated building letters, a custom pylon sign carrying the plaza logo and the resident brand display, the garage entrance signage, interior suspended directional signs and floor directory totems, functional space signage for restrooms, lifts and the information desk, and brand extension elements including the illuminated logo work.

##### What materials and processes were used?

The system was produced in stainless steel and acrylic. The fabrication route covers laser cutting, seamless welding, powder coating and illuminated fabrication, which is what allows the outdoor elements and the interior signs to share the same finish.

##### Why does the pylon sign carry both branding and wayfinding?

The pylon stands where a visitor is deciding whether to turn in. Combining the plaza logo, an illuminated display of the resident brands and wayfinding graphics on one structure answers the identity question and the orientation question at the same point, rather than making the visitor read two separate signs.

##### Why is the garage entrance signage designed as one assembly?

A driver meets the entrance name, the plaza logo, the height restriction, the speed limit and the no-horn requirement while moving. Bringing them onto a single unit keeps one decision in one place instead of splitting it across panels the driver passes at speed.

##### Can ZYD deliver a comparable wayfinding package for another mall?

Yes. The scope covers design development, production, installation and commissioning, with DDP shipping for export projects.

### Dongguan Street | Heritage Signage and Themed Installations

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/dongguan-street-dalian-heritage-renewal
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/dongguan-street-dalian-heritage-renewal/index.md

A hundred-year-old street in Dalian, China, was renewed as a commercial and cultural district. ZYD Signage designed and produced the wayfinding system that makes the lanes legible and the themed installations that give the heritage frontages a second life.

Heritage / Mixed Use • Dalian, China • Wayfinding + Themed Installations

![Giant gold bow installation tied over the corner of a red brick Dongguan Street building, with scalloped window hoods and flower boxes along the facade](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-giant-gold-bow-installation.jpg)

*A giant gold bow tied over the corner of the Dongguan Street brick building.*

The renewal was delivered as two bodies of work on one street. The wayfinding system gives the lanes a hierarchy of direction, attraction and event information in a black and orange palette with bilingual Chinese and English lettering; the installation programme adds a flower-dressed street, a burst of red balloons, a National Geographic display set, the No.15 Courtyard identity with its heritage craft market, and a giant bow over the brick corner, all designed to respect the historic buildings they sit against.

#### Project facts

#### Part one - wayfinding system: making a historic street legible

A street of connected lanes needs a system rather than a set of individual signs. The wayfinding for Dongguan Street was designed in a simple, contemporary language that sits against the restored fabric of the street, and it was planned for both practical direction and appearance.

Localised design language: black and orange were used as the main colours, echoing the red brick and warm lighting of the street, with bilingual Chinese and English lettering and clear pictograms so that residents and visitors from out of town can read the same information.

Function and setting combined: the signs were planned against the street circulation as a multi-level set, presenting attractions, retail and public facilities together, while low-saturation colours keep them in keeping with the buildings rather than competing with them.

Detail carrying the culture: the wave pattern at the base of the signs is drawn from Dalian's maritime character, which puts a piece of the city into the smallest part of the wayfinding.

![Illuminated visitor centre lettering in Chinese mounted on the dark stone archway of a restored building on Dongguan Street](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-visitor-centre-illuminated-letters.jpg)

*Illuminated lettering set into the stone archway of the visitor centre.*

![Freestanding double-post notice frame holding a glass-fronted poster panel on the paved street in front of a stone-clad building](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-freestanding-notice-frame.jpg)

*A freestanding frame for tenant and event notices, detailed to sit on the street surface.*

![Freestanding three-panel directory board at night showing coupon offers, member benefits and an activity calendar below a street name band](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-directory-board-at-night.jpg)

*The three-panel directory board carrying offers, member information and the event calendar.*

#### Part two - themed installations: giving the street a second life

If wayfinding is the skeleton of the street, the installations are its expression. Several photo points were created along Dongguan Street with a mix of ideas, so that a historic district has a young, lively voice.

![Vertical illuminated blade sign with the street name in white Chinese characters on a black panel, mounted on a red brick corner beside a street lamp at night](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-illuminated-blade-sign-at-night.jpg)

*A vertical blade sign on the brick corner, read along the street rather than across it.*

![Cluster of red balloon spheres bursting out from the wall of a beige rendered heritage building, with red ribbons hanging below](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-red-balloon-installation.jpg)

*The balloon cluster breaking out of the facade, with ribbons carrying the colour down to street level.*

##### 1. Flower-dressed street: the romantic devices

Working from the idea of abundant flowers, several landmark devices were made so that the old street is wrapped gently rather than decorated heavily.

- Street lamp floral device: vintage street lamps were wrapped in colourful artificial flowers, with bouquets grading from orange and yellow into pink and purple. The devices give the corners a romantic mood, and when the lamps come on in the evening the flower shapes and the warm light interweave.
- Red balloon device: clusters of red balloons fly out from the building wall. The strong colour contrasts with the warm beige facade, giving the street a storybook quality and a recognisable photo point.
- Music note floral device: working from a music note and a painter's palette with multicoloured flower clusters, the piece brings an artistic note into a street corner and answers the artistic character of the district.

![National Geographic themed installation with tilted yellow photo frames, a portrait photograph and cut-out letters reading Born To Shine, lit from the base](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-national-geographic-installation.jpg)

*The National Geographic display: yellow frames at staggered angles around a portrait image and the BORN TO SHINE lettering.*

![Red funnel sculpture on a post pouring a stream of pink roses up and across the brick and stone facade of a heritage building at night, with a person leaning into the funnel](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-rose-funnel-floral-installation.jpg)

*The funnel device: a stream of roses poured up the brick facade, built to be stood beside and photographed.*

##### 2. Themed IP: telling the street's story in scenes

Responding to the cultural position of the district, several themed sets were made so that the story of the lanes has a visible form.

- National Geographic exhibition: the signature yellow frame was used as the design element, built as a three-dimensional set at staggered angles, combining classic photographic work with the BORN TO SHINE theme, which gives the street a human and artistic layer.
- Cultural commercial installation: working with the heritage craft market and the individual tenants along the street, the No.15 Courtyard leap over the dragon gate identity and the market stall devices were made, bringing Dalian's intangible cultural heritage together with the commercial frontage so that the signs carry a local warmth as well as identifying the businesses.
- Giant bow device: a large gold bow was tied onto the red brick building, softening the hard lines of the old architecture and giving the street a ceremonial, playful note that has become one of its signature images.

![Shop facade on Dongguan Street with an illuminated red dragon medallion, red koi and blue cloud motifs set around illuminated Chinese shop lettering](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-courtyard-dragon-gate-facade.jpg)

*The No.15 Courtyard shopfront: dragon medallion, koi and cloud motifs around the illuminated shop name.*

![Giant gold bow installation tied over the corner of a red brick heritage building, with scalloped window hoods and window flower boxes along the facade](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-giant-gold-bow-installation.jpg)

*The oversized bow tied over the corner of the brick building, softening the roofline.*

#### Part three - design approach: balancing the historic and the present

The renewal of Dongguan Street is not a replacement of its history but a continuation and revival of the culture of the place.

Supporting cast rather than lead role: every sign and installation was designed on the premise of respecting the fabric of the historic buildings. Colour, material and form were matched to the period atmosphere of the street, so the devices read as the supporting cast of the lanes and not as the main event.

Culture that can be felt, scenes that can be entered: whether it is the maritime element in the wayfinding or the local cultural expression in the installations, the intention is that the design does more than look good, and that a visitor can read the character of the city and the history of the street while using it.

Suited to more than one occasion: from commercial identity to public installation, and from everyday use to event programming, the design serves both the cultural tourism role of the district and the commercial needs of its tenants, which is what gives the street a scene that can last.

A hundred years of Dongguan Street is half sediment of history and half vitality of renewal. Guiding the footsteps with wayfinding and lighting the lanes with installations is how the conversation between the historic and the present is held, and how memories of the city live alongside a younger mood.

![Yellow illuminated ring framing an arched window in a red brick wall, dressed with greenery, moss and pink and orange flowers](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-floral-arch-window.jpg)

*A window arch dressed with flowers around an illuminated ring, turning a blank opening into a viewing point.*

![Street tree in blossom with hanging floral decorations and an illuminated yellow rose with a music note outline standing in a bed of red, blue and yellow flowers](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-music-note-floral-tree.jpg)

*The music note and rose piece at the foot of a street tree, with the flower bed carrying the colour.*

![Red teahouse ticket pavilion on Dongguan Street with a tiled roof detail, illuminated Chinese lettering and a green sign reading there are stories here](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-teahouse-pavilion.jpg)

*The teahouse ticket pavilion, built as a small roofed structure against the brick elevation.*

![Strings of festoon lights, glass globes and printed pennant flags spanning the street between restored brick shopfronts at dusk](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-festoon-light-canopy.jpg)

*Festoon lighting and printed pennants spanning the street, carrying the street name across the frontages.*

![Blue heritage craft market stall with gold trim, dragon motifs and Chinese lettering for a sugar-figure demonstration, in front of a lit brick facade](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/dongguan-street-heritage-craft-stall-pavilion.jpg)

*A heritage craft stall in the market set, drawn from the same blue and gold palette as the shopfront signs.*

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What did the Dongguan Street renewal cover?

Two bodies of work along one street: a wayfinding signage system with direction, attraction and event information, and a themed installation programme with floral devices, a balloon device, a National Geographic display set, cultural commercial installations tied to the heritage craft market, and a large bow on the brick facade.

##### How is wayfinding designed for a historic street?

By planning the signs against the street circulation as a multi-level set, then choosing a language that leaves the architecture in charge: here a black and orange palette echoing the red brick and warm lighting, bilingual Chinese and English lettering with clear pictograms, low-saturation colours, and a coastline wave pattern at the base of the signs as a local detail.

##### How are themed installations chosen for a heritage district?

Each one is chosen to create a photo point and to speak about the place: floral devices wrapped around street lamps, a balloon cluster flying out of a facade, a music note and palette piece, a National Geographic frame set, the No.15 Courtyard dragon gate identity with the heritage craft market stalls, and the gold bow on the building corner.

##### How do the installations avoid overpowering the old buildings?

Every element is designed on the basis of respecting the fabric of the historic buildings. Colour, material and form are matched to the period atmosphere of the street, so the devices work as the supporting cast of the lanes, and the low-saturation choices in the signage keep the wayfinding from competing with the architecture.

##### Can the same approach be used on another street or district?

The method transfers, the palette does not. The design language here was drawn from Dalian's maritime character and from the history of the street itself, and the installation set was coordinated with the tenant mix and the cultural programming. A comparable brief starts from the history of that place and the way the district needs to be used.

### Hengli Industrial Park Wayfinding Signage

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/hengli-industrial-park-wayfinding-signage
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/hengli-industrial-park-wayfinding-signage/index.md

A large industrial park needed one wayfinding and signage system for its gateway, roads, buildings, production zones and functional spaces. ZYD Signage planned the hierarchy, produced the signage and coordinated site installation and after-sales maintenance.

Large Industrial Park • Bilingual Wayfinding • Stainless Steel Signage

![Illuminated entrance image wall at Hengli Industrial Park carrying the park name in dimensional lettering beside a circular park logo](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-entrance-image-wall.jpg)

*Illuminated entrance image wall at the Hengli Industrial Park gateway.*

Hengli Industrial Park uses a graded wayfinding system to connect the entrance identity, road zones, building numbers, production workshop areas and everyday functional signs. Stainless steel construction, bilingual information and coordinated planning support a clear visual language across the industrial setting.

#### Project facts

#### The challenge: one system for a large industrial park

Hengli Industrial Park brings together offices, accommodation, production workshops, roads, landscaped areas and operational facilities. A visitor, employee or vehicle needs a clear route through a site with different zones and different movement patterns.

The signage therefore needs to do more than identify individual buildings. It needs to establish a visual and wayfinding order across the park, while keeping people and vehicles moving through the right areas.

- Create a clear sequence from the park entrance to roads, buildings and internal destinations.
- Separate people and vehicle movement through road-zone and facility information.
- Keep gateway, accommodation, office, workshop and functional signs visually related.
- Use bilingual Chinese and English information where visitors and teams need it.

#### A graded wayfinding structure from gateway to destination

The system follows a graded sequence: the entrance establishes the park identity, road signs divide the movement network, building numbers and door signs identify destinations, workshop markers define production zones, and functional signs support everyday operations.

This hierarchy gives each sign a clear role. A large gateway element is read from the approach, while a building number, workshop zone marker or functional sign is read at a closer decision point.

#### Gateway identity and landscape signage

The park entrance is the first identity point in the system. A curved image wall carries the park name in large dimensional lettering, paired with a circular logo element, so the gateway reads as one composition from the approach road.

A second entrance treatment sets freestanding park name letters into the landscaped lawn. Both parts establish the visual language that continues into the road, building and production-area signs across Hengli Industrial Park.

![Large freestanding park name letters on the lawn at the Hengli Industrial Park entrance, with the bilingual welcome line beneath](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-entrance-landscape-letters.jpg)

*Large freestanding park name letters on the lawn at the Hengli Industrial Park entrance, with the bilingual welcome line beneath*

#### Building numbers and campus identification

The accommodation and office side of the park is read at a closer distance than the entrance. Building number signs mounted on the facades identify individual blocks, and the number sits on the brick elevation itself rather than on a separate board.

Because the buildings share one architectural language, the number signs carry the identification role. That keeps the campus legible floor by floor without adding signage clutter to the elevations.

![Accommodation and office buildings at Hengli Industrial Park seen from above, with landscaped grounds and parking between them](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-campus-buildings.jpg)

*Accommodation and office buildings at Hengli Industrial Park seen from above, with landscaped grounds and parking between them*

![Building number sign mounted on a brick facade at Hengli Industrial Park](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-building-number-sign.jpg)

*Building number sign mounted on a brick facade at Hengli Industrial Park*

#### Production workshop zone signage

The production area operates at a different scale from the rest of the park. Workshop facades carry identification signs set high on the cladding, and zone plates mark the subdivisions within a single workshop building.

Workshop zone markers therefore have to work from a distance and at the building line. The signs identify the workshop and its production zone so that teams and vehicles move to the correct part of the structure.

![Production workshop building at Hengli Industrial Park with an identification sign mounted high on the facade cladding](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-future-factory-building.jpg)

*Production workshop building at Hengli Industrial Park with an identification sign mounted high on the facade cladding*

![Workshop wall sign identifying a production zone at Hengli Industrial Park, with a separate zone plate fixed below it](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-workshop-zone-sign.jpg)

*Workshop wall sign identifying a production zone at Hengli Industrial Park, with a separate zone plate fixed below it*

![Steel structure and overhead crane of a large production workshop at Hengli Industrial Park during construction](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-workshop-steel-structure.jpg)

*Steel structure and overhead crane of a large production workshop at Hengli Industrial Park during construction*

#### Road zones and people and vehicle movement

The workshops sit either side of internal site roads, with crossing markings carrying pedestrian movement across the vehicle route. Road-zone information and the building signs work together at these points, so a driver or a pedestrian reads direction before committing to a turn.

This is where separating people and vehicle movement matters most. The road layout, the crossing markings and the adjacent building identification combine into one readable route rather than three separate cues.

![Two large production workshops at Hengli Industrial Park facing each other across a site road with crossing markings](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-workshop-road.jpg)

*Two large production workshops at Hengli Industrial Park facing each other across a site road with crossing markings*

#### Functional signage with bilingual information

Functional signs cover the everyday points that need quick recognition, including fire-safety locations, equipment spaces, service facilities and rest areas. Clear symbols and bilingual Chinese and English wording help the signs work for different users across the park.

Freestanding directional signs carry facility information into the landscaped areas, so a visitor can locate a service point from the road or path rather than only at the building door.

![Freestanding property service centre directional sign in the landscaped grounds at Hengli Industrial Park](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/hengli-industrial-park-property-service-centre-sign.jpg)

*Freestanding property service centre directional sign in the landscaped grounds at Hengli Industrial Park*

#### Materials and fabrication for an industrial setting

Stainless steel forms the base for the signage elements, with the fabrication route using laser cutting and CNC bending to create clean, repeatable forms. Screen printing supports the information graphics, while weather-resistant coatings protect the exterior finish.

For illuminated elements, waterproof and dust-resistant LED modules are used within the sign construction. The material and process choices are matched to the different conditions of gateways, roads, buildings, workshops and functional spaces.

- Stainless steel base materials for signage elements and related metalwork.
- Laser cutting and CNC bending for controlled shapes and lettering.
- Screen printing for clear information graphics.
- Weather-resistant coatings for exterior applications.
- Waterproof and dust-resistant LED modules for illuminated signs.

#### Survey, production and site delivery

The delivery route starts with a full-site survey and graded wayfinding planning. The information structure is then translated into factory production, followed by coordinated installation across the park areas.

After installation, the service scope includes after-sales maintenance. This keeps the system supported beyond the initial production and site installation stages.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What does the Hengli Industrial Park signage system cover?

It covers the park gateway, road zones, people and vehicle movement, accommodation and office building numbers, door signs, production workshop areas, and functional signs for fire-safety, equipment and rest spaces.

##### Is the signage bilingual?

The system uses Chinese and English bilingual information where the park wayfinding and functional signs need to communicate with different users.

##### What materials and processes are used?

The signage uses stainless steel elements with laser cutting, CNC bending, screen printing and weather-resistant coatings. Illuminated signs use waterproof and dust-resistant LED modules within the sign construction.

##### How is a large industrial park signage project delivered?

The service begins with a full-site survey and graded planning, continues through factory production and site installation, and includes after-sales maintenance.

### Pavilion Dalian | Festive Installations Driving Footfall

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/pavilion-dalian-mall-festive-installations
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/case-studies/pavilion-dalian-mall-festive-installations/index.md

A multi-level shopping centre in Dalian, China, needed Christmas and Lunar New Year atrium installations that read as one identity across every gallery level, could be suspended safely above a trading floor, and could be installed at night without disrupting tenants. ZYD Signage designed, manufactured and installed them.

Retail / Shopping Centre • Dalian, China • Seasonal Atrium Installations

![Shopping centre atrium at Christmas with a candy-themed installation of illuminated lollipops, doughnuts and an ice cream cone suspended around a fir tree](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-christmas-candy-installation.webp)

*Sweet-themed pieces suspended at staggered heights around the illuminated tree in the atrium.*

ZYD Signage delivered the festive installation programme for Pavilion Dalian, a shopping centre in Dalian, China. The work covered a Christmas presentation and a Lunar New Year presentation, each built as a set of floor and suspended installations distributed through a tall voided atrium, from theme concept and 3D development through steel and acrylic fabrication, lighting integration, night-time installation and post-season clearance.

#### Project facts

#### Project background: why a mall atrium needs a seasonal installation programme

Pavilion Dalian is a shopping centre in Dalian, China, with retail and leisure floors arranged around a tall voided atrium. The atrium is the point where visitors on several gallery levels see the same space at once, which makes it the most valuable seasonal display area in the building and the hardest one to install into.

The brief covered the centre's major festive periods rather than a single event: a Christmas presentation and a Lunar New Year presentation, each built as a set of installations distributed through the atrium instead of one object on the floor.

For a shopping centre, the work is judged on three things at the same time: whether the installation reads as one identity across levels, whether it is safe to suspend above a trading floor, and whether it can be built and removed without disrupting tenants.

![Multi-level shopping centre atrium seen from above with a Christmas tree, carousel and suspended sweet-themed decorations](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-atrium-christmas-overview.webp)

*Multi-level shopping centre atrium seen from above with a Christmas tree, carousel and suspended sweet-themed decorations*

#### What the brief had to solve

Four issues shaped the programme. Each one was addressed at design and fabrication stage rather than on site.

- Fragmented festive identity: installations supplied separately for each period can look and light differently. The response was a single visual specification for the year, with the centre's own identity carried into the installation graphics so consecutive campaigns read as one series.
- Suspended load above a public floor: large hanging elements over a voided atrium need a structure designed for them. Purpose-built load-bearing frames were fabricated for the suspended elements, with structural verification of the hanging assemblies and protected low-voltage LED wiring, and the works were coordinated with the property and fire-safety acceptance process.
- Tight festive calendar and trading hours: the festive window is fixed and the atrium cannot be closed for long. Components were prefabricated as modules in the factory so site work became assembly, and installation was scheduled at night outside trading hours.
- Dual exposure and daily contact: outdoor elements face weather while atrium pieces are touched by visitors every day. Outdoor elements were built in weather-resistant coated metal, indoor sculptural elements used thickened acrylic and sheet metal, and lighting was supplied as integrated modules.

#### Christmas presentation: a distributed atrium installation

The Christmas scheme centred on a large illuminated tree and then spread outward, so visitors on upper gallery levels still had something to look at. Sweet-themed hanging pieces &mdash; lollipops, doughnuts, candy canes and an ice cream cone &mdash; were suspended at staggered heights around the tree, with illuminated rides and figures on the atrium floor.

Laying the scheme out in layers was a deliberate choice. A single centrepiece reads well only from the ground floor, whereas distributing elements vertically gives every gallery level a usable view and spreads visitor movement through the space.

The same installation supported the centre's own seasonal programme: the staging area in the atrium was used for performances and events, so the display had to leave circulation space and support event use rather than occupy the floor.

![Close view of a large illuminated carousel wheel installation with pink, purple and green steel rings on a shopping centre atrium floor](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-carousel-wheel-installation.webp)

*Close view of a large illuminated carousel wheel installation with pink, purple and green steel rings on a shopping centre atrium floor*

![Shoppers gathered on the ground floor of a shopping centre atrium around illuminated Christmas installations and a light-up reindeer](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-atrium-visitor-activation.webp)

*Shoppers gathered on the ground floor of a shopping centre atrium around illuminated Christmas installations and a light-up reindeer*

#### Lunar New Year presentation: traditional forms in a modern atrium

The New Year scheme worked in red and gold. A gilded bull sculpture stood on a podium as the floor-level anchor, surrounded by illuminated fan shapes, while red lanterns were distributed through the void above so the colour reads from every gallery.

Rather than reproducing traditional objects at domestic scale, the elements were scaled to the building. Lanterns were sized and spaced to register from three or four levels away, and the podium was designed as a complete floor object with integrated lighting rather than a sculpture placed on a plinth.

The two programmes share a layout logic even though the palettes differ. That consistency is what allows the centre to run consecutive campaigns in the same space without rebuilding the visual identity each time.

![Lunar New Year installation in a shopping centre atrium with a gilded bull sculpture on a red podium, red lanterns and illuminated fan shapes](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-lunar-new-year-bull-lanterns.webp)

*Lunar New Year installation in a shopping centre atrium with a gilded bull sculpture on a red podium, red lanterns and illuminated fan shapes*

![View down through four levels of a shopping centre atrium filled with red Lunar New Year lanterns, hanging banners and a gilded bull centrepiece](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-new-year-atrium-overview.webp)

*View down through four levels of a shopping centre atrium filled with red Lunar New Year lanterns, hanging banners and a gilded bull centrepiece*

#### Suspended decoration system for a high voided atrium

The suspended layer is the part of the programme that distinguishes a high-atrium installation from ordinary shop-floor dressing. Decorations were custom fabricated as star, fan and festive lantern-box forms and hung in multiple tiers below the roof structure.

Suspension points, drop lengths and clearances were planned as a system so the elements sit at consistent heights relative to each gallery, filling the vertical volume that would otherwise read as empty space. Tall suspended lattice lantern columns were used in the New Year scheme to carry the eye upward between shopfronts.

Because access to these elements after installation is limited, the hanging hardware and wiring for each unit were completed and checked at the factory before the unit was lifted into place.

![Aerial view of suspended red Lunar New Year lanterns and themed hanging decorations distributed across a shopping centre atrium](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-new-year-hanging-lanterns.webp)

*Aerial view of suspended red Lunar New Year lanterns and themed hanging decorations distributed across a shopping centre atrium*

![Tall suspended red lattice lantern columns hanging from the roof structure above the shopfronts of a shopping centre atrium](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-suspended-lantern-columns.webp)

*Tall suspended red lattice lantern columns hanging from the roof structure above the shopfronts of a shopping centre atrium*

#### Structure, materials and lighting approach

The installations are built objects, not props. Structural framing was fabricated specifically for the loads and fixing points of each element, and outdoor pieces used weather-resistant coated metal so the same scheme can run through a full winter season.

Lighting is integrated into the structures rather than added afterwards, with wiring routed and protected as part of the assembly and low-voltage LED used throughout the suspended elements. Materials were chosen by location: outdoor elements for exposure, indoor sculptural work in thickened acrylic and sheet metal where visitors can touch them.

Fabrication was split between the factory and the site on purpose. Structures, sculptural forms and lighting assemblies were produced and pre-assembled off site so the on-site phase was reduced to positioning, connection and finishing.

![Children performing on a staging area inside a shopping centre atrium beneath a large illuminated Christmas tree, watched by a crowd](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-christmas-stage-performance.webp)

*Children performing on a staging area inside a shopping centre atrium beneath a large illuminated Christmas tree, watched by a crowd*

![View down through the galleried atrium of a shopping centre showing a suspended carousel wheel, Christmas tree and hanging tenant banners across six levels](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/projects/pavilion-dalian-atrium-multi-level-overview.webp)

*View down through the galleried atrium of a shopping centre showing a suspended carousel wheel, Christmas tree and hanging tenant banners across six levels*

#### How the delivery chain ran

The programme followed one sequence from concept to clearance, which is what allows a centre to keep its atrium continuously in use:

- Theme concept and creative direction for the festive period.
- 3D visual development to agree scale, layout and appearance with the centre before production.
- Sheet metal and acrylic production of the sculptural and structural elements.
- Custom lighting integration and factory pre-assembly of suspended units.
- Night-time installation and assembly inside the trading centre.
- Removal and site clearance at the end of the festive period.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What does a shopping centre festive installation programme include?

A programme of this type normally covers creative concept and 3D development, structural fabrication for floor and suspended elements, custom lighting integration, off-site pre-assembly, night-time installation inside the trading centre, and removal and clearance when the festive period ends.

##### How are decorations suspended safely above a shopping centre atrium?

Suspended elements need their own load-bearing framing rather than being hung from whatever is available. On this project the hanging assemblies were fabricated for the loads and fixing points involved, structurally verified, and fitted with protected low-voltage LED wiring, with the works coordinated through the property and fire-safety acceptance process.

##### How is installation arranged so shops can keep trading?

By moving as much of the build as possible into the factory. Components are produced and pre-assembled as modules off site, so the on-site phase is assembly and positioning rather than fabrication, and that work can be scheduled at night outside trading hours.

##### Which materials suit outdoor and indoor festive installations?

Exposure drives the choice. Outdoor elements here used weather-resistant coated metal, while indoor sculptural work used thickened acrylic and sheet metal because it is handled and touched daily. Lighting was supplied as integrated modules rather than added as a separate operation.

### ZYD Signage について

Canonical page: https://www.zydsign.com/ja/about
Markdown mirror: https://www.zydsign.com/ja/about/index.md

2006年から、精密なものづくりで国際サイネージ業界をリードしています。

大連志宇道（Dalian Zhiyudao Signage & Tech. Co., Ltd.／ZYD）は、2006年から世界のB2Bサイネージ案件を手がける工場直送メーカーです。

20,000m²の生産拠点にCNC加工設備と体系化された生産工程を備え、建築導線サインやオーダーメイドサインを製作しています。

納品先と貨物の情報が確定した段階で、Door-to-Door（DDP）配送のお見積もりが可能です。合意する納品範囲、関税、税金はプロジェクトごとの見積もりによって決まります。

![ZYD Signage の工場入口](https://www.zydsign.com/assets/images/company-entrance.jpg)

工場入口

#### 工場で製作しているもの

建築導線サインと点字サイン、医療施設向けサイン、ハロー（背面発光）金属文字、超薄型LEDライトボックス、LEDネオン、金属・アクリルロゴサイン、屋外ピロン・モニュメントサイン、ランドスケープ家具、屋外ゴミ箱、プランター、アクリル卓上サイン、金属製A型看板、そして統合サイネージシステムまでを一つの工場で製作しています。一つの案件で複数の種類を同時に発注いただくことが多いため、図面も納品範囲もまとめて管理できる体制にしています。各製品は[製品一覧](https://www.zydsign.com/ja/products) でご案内しています。

素材は304ステンレス、溶融亜鉛めっき鋼、アルミニウムを中心に、アクリルとLED部材を組み合わせます。板金は1.5mmの板材から加工し、塗装は180℃の焼付塗装で仕上げます。いずれも加工の条件を示すもので、性能の指標ではありません。どの素材ルートと仕上げを採るかは、サインが設置される環境に合わせて案件ごとに決めます。

#### 案件が工場を流れる順序

すべてのご注文は同じ8段階で進み、各段階でお客様が確認できる成果物が生まれます。技術相談、3Dモックアップ、施工図、加工、塗装、LED組込、品質確認、そして梱包・出荷です。図面が確定する前に生産へ回すことはありません。

1. 01技術相談サイネージのご要望と設置条件を分析します。
2. 02精密3Dモックアップ仕上がりを3Dで確認いただきます。
3. 03施工図（ショップドローイング）構造と電気系統の詳細図面を作成します。
4. 04CNC加工高精度な切断と組立を行います。
5. 05塗装設置環境に合わせた仕上げを施します。
6. 06LED組込仕様に合わせたLEDモジュールと配線を組み込みます。
7. 07点灯検査点灯試験を含む工程ごとの品質確認を行います。
8. 08世界DDP配送工業用梱包とdoor-to-doorの物流を手配します。

#### 品質の確認方法

品質は最後の一度の検査ではなく、取り決めた確認項目の積み重ねとして扱います。以下の4点をお客様と取り決め、案件ごとに記録します。これにより、供給側とお客様が同じ範囲を見ている状態になります。

- 品質管理工程を案件ごとに確認します。
- 電気要件納品先の条件に照らして確認します。
- 検査範囲生産前に取り決めます。
- 部材選定仕様に合わせて選定します。

#### ご発注と配送について

最小ロットは1台です。受付カウンターのサイン1台から、複数拠点への展開まで承ります。通常の生産リードタイムは内容と数量により7〜14日で、図面とアートワークが確定した時点から起算します。

納品先と貨物の情報が確定した段階で、DDPをdoor-to-doorの範囲としてお見積もりできます。合意する納品範囲、関税・税金、保証の範囲・期間・除外事項は、案件ごとの見積書または供給契約に記載します。

アートワークとブランド資料は見積もり前に確認し、3Dモックアップの段階で仕上がりの方向性をご確認いただきます。確定している図面や条件をそのままに、[お問い合わせフォーム](https://www.zydsign.com/ja/contact) からご相談ください。

Before You Write

#### お見積もりに必要な情報

サイネージのお見積もりは製品名ではなく案件の内容から組み立てるため、すでに確定している条件をうかがえると、比較できる価格に最短で到達します。同じ範囲を同じ前提で見積もることができ、未確定の項目も未確定のまま共有できます。

今お手元にあるものだけで構いません。おおよその寸法、設置面の写真、ロゴデータがあれば検討を始められます。図面は技術相談の中で一緒に詰めていき、無料の3Dモックアップで仕上がりを確認してから製作に入ります。

最小ロットは1台、通常の生産リードタイムは図面とアートワークの確定後7〜14日です。情報が揃わない場合は、生産の着手が遅れるだけで、お見積もりの検討は進められます。よくあるご質問は[FAQ・資料](https://www.zydsign.com/ja/faq) にまとめています。

##### 案件情報チェックリスト

- アートワークまたはロゴデータ（ブランドカラーの指定があれば併せて）
- サインの種類、未定の場合は設置場所と伝えたい内容
- おおよその寸法・文字の高さ・数量
- 屋内か屋外か、および取付面の状況
- 照明のご希望（前面発光・背面発光・照明なし・未定）
- 素材と仕上げのご指定があればその方向性
- 設置場所の写真と、搬入・取付の制約
- 設置先の都市と国、納品先、ご希望の時期

不明な項目は「未定」のままで構いません。技術検討の中で確認し、推測で埋めることはしません。
